title: Great in theory! Not for me in execution
body: I tried to give feedback on the app but there wasn’t a user friendly way to do so. While I absolutely love the premise of this app- in the 3 days I’ve downloaded it the amount of notifications it gives you is overwhelming. I built in my routine and set what / when I wanted to be notified. And yes I got those but I also received about 15 other notifications from it daily. It also has a vary cartoonish design which is cute but not nearly as customizable as I would like. It attempts to be a one stop shop for you but doesn’t integrate food tracking or your calendar easily. It allows for hydration tracking but even that isn’t the easiest. This app may be great for a younger generation that enjoys being chronically online but for someone looking to simply set and forget until the notifications/reminders you specifically set go off - it’s too much. I want an app that’ll LOWER my screen time, not ding almost every hour to check it. Wanted to love it but ended up deleting it.

title: All over the place
body: If you have ADHD or, OCD this is not the app for you. The concept is good but unfortunately after you enter all your morning, noon, evening tasks to do. When you go into your list to check off the task it’s not in the order you entered them. I even tried setting a time for each task and the task will be set wherever. You have to go hunting for your task. The task will not be in the order you want them no matter how you set them up. Even tried the morning, afternoon, evening tabs and go into each tab separately. Nope all my task are all over the place. So if I have a task to complete in the morning, another in the evening, three in the afternoon. The tasks will be all over the place and you have to go searching each one individually if you remember which one they were. The app will give you anxiety and make your ADHD worse. I reached out the developer and received an email it’s a glitch and they are working on it. I asked for a refund and they went silent. Never responded to my email after that. Refund policy is a lie. I had to let the app sit on my phone for almost a year because I paid for a year subscription with no use. I will go in the app from time and time to see if they fixed the glitch and they haven’t. I think people on here leaving positive feedback either are paid to do so, or their lives must be just as disarrayed as the app is and they don’t mind. But for someone who has ADHD, OCD, or like organization in their lives this is not the app for you.

title: Very helpful, wish we could add multiple tags
body:
Over all, I really like this app. Unlike a lot of habit/routine trackers, it doesn’t lock crucial features like customized repeating days, tagging categories, or the number of tasks you can add behind a paywall. I love that the widgets help to visualize your progress, both in terms of task streaks and with a percentage bar of what you’ve finished that day. 

The ability to add one-off tasks if you want to use this as a to-do list is also nice, even if I don’t personally use it that way. 

I don’t love the premium add popup every time I open the app, but for a free app that’s really not bad at all. 

I do, however, REALLY wish we could give habits/tasks multiple tags. EG. Stretching is both part of my morning routine AND part of my health/fitness journey, so it would be nice to be able to see it under both filters. Honestly if that was an option I would absolutely go up to 5 stars. If there’s somewhere to submit feature requests I would love to know.

title: Good So Far, but…
body: So far, I’m enjoying the app and all of this features. I do like the focus of the app. One thing that I do think was overlooked was inclusiveness with the diversity of the characters and icon choices. I wish there were options for people of color. For some that might not seem like much but the feeling of not being represented does play on one’s mental health. Being that this is a mental health and well-being based app and that there are features for you to share this information with your community, not being able to see yourself in the visualizers decreases one’s mental health. I think that is something worth looking into the same way phones icons can be switched to different skin tones. I wanted to share one of the routine charts with my community, but none of the images looks like anyone in my community. That made me anxious. Other than that, the app itself is very good. Thank you.

title: Better for Tasks Than Routines
body:
I have purchased subscriptions to several apps relating to routines/tasks. None of them are exactly what I want, including Me+. I wish I could combine the functions of several of the routine/task apps to create exactly what I want. 

Me+ has some great features. It is colorful and easy to read. I like how it allows you to set a time period as opposed to a specific time for performance of a task. I like that you are able to go to a particular date in the future and see each task (or routine) that you need to complete on that particular date. I wish it had some options  for repetitive tasks like the first, second, third, fourth, and last “day of the week” in a month. I also wish it had some seasonal, quarterly, and semi-annual options for repetitive tasks. 

The tags make it easy to group particular tasks.  One of the ways that you can create a routine is by using the same tag on each task of the routine. You can edit the order of the tasks as you refine or add to your routine. However, as a mother, I have multiple routines that I need to run each morning. The use of only tags to name and compile the tasks in a routine the creates the potential for a lot of tags. In the calendar view, the tabs with the tags are displayed in alphabetical order instead of chronological order, which makes it cumbersome to find routines that you need to perform in a certain order. 

One of the ways that you could potentially address this issue is to set up a routine by naming a task as a routine. Then, within the task, you can identify subtasks. The app specifically states that “[s]ubtasks can be set as your daily routine or checklist.” However, you cannot edit the order of the subtasks, so if you decide to add something to a routine or change the order in which you perform the routine, you cannot reorder your list. Therefore, out-of-order subtasks effectively become a “checklist.”Therefore, in my view, Me+ is better as a task app than an actual routine app. 

I like that completed tasks are scratched and moved to the bottom of the list because it better enables you to focus on your remaining tasks at the top of the list. However, I wish Me+ allowed tasks that you deliberately mark as skipped to move to the bottom of the list so you could better focus on the remaining tasks that you are not skipping. Skipping creates clutter at the top of the list.

I like that Me+ does not force you to “time box” each task or subtask because sometimes you must complete everything regardless of how long it takes. Yet, I also wish Me+ allowed you to set a time box for specific tasks and subtasks. If you need to time box within a routine, Routinery is a much better app for you. The drawback is that Routinery requires you to set a time box for every single task within a routine, so I am not completely satisfied with either app. 

Me+ allows you to change the tag on a task, but it does not allow you to edit the actual tags. This is a problem if you misspell a tag or want to improve the name of a tag.  A mistake or improvement will require you to create a new tag and then retag each task with the inaccurate tag. You also cannot change the order of the tags in the list of tags, which becomes cumbersome if you have a large list of tags. In short, there needs to be a better editing function for tags.

I enjoy several features in Me+. Yet, I am not really sold on it for the price of the subscription as a true routine app.

title: Game Changer
body:
I LOVE this app. I’ve been using it for about 4 years now. I’ve watched it go through many different formats/changes and I’ve loved it every step of the way. I can tell the developers are constantly trying to come up with ways to better it and it’s amazing. As someone with undiagnosed ADHD/Autism I struggle with knowing what to do next sometimes & staying on task/productive. This app has guided me through many phases of life and helped me achieve my goals in ways I never thought possible. I’m able to clearly outline the habits I need to achieve my goals and even my chores and morning routines. It makes being productive feel like a game, with a colorful, mood-lifting layout and endless ways to customize your routines. And if you don’t know where to start the resources they provide to guide you are phenomenal. I personally love the finance routine, it’s so helpful. I’ve tried to get through my routines without it and it is just not the same. It’s great to have everything I need to do/my ideas in one app. It encourages consistent, healthy daily habits and when you follow through on that kind of thing it really is life-changing. Cannot recommend this app enough, I’ve told many friends about it lol. I don’t have premium right now but I have in the past. Seems to still be very user-friendly and accessible even if you can’t afford premium yet. 
Thank you Me+!!!! 😄😆😍💜

title: Cost is $59.99 for a year
body:
The description say the cost is $29.99 is a lie. Their inattention to that detail tells you all you need to know about this app.

The next issue is with the English in some videos. I’m a bit surprised that the actors and actresses don’t correct the flaws. For example, the welcome video says uses the wrong word when they meant to say “aboard”. 

Nothing presented in this app is based on science. None of the psychology, none of the routines for neurodivergent people, not the exercises, nothing.

There is no explanation of what the “AI” is in the app or how your information is stored or if it is shared. They claim that they can use a picture of your bedroom to generate a cleaning list. All that you get from sharing that intimate a picture is a generic list. 

The Finch app is better for mental health. The Sweepy app is better for home stuff.

In response to the developer response - no, I’m not going to email you my issues. It’s not my job to get feedback to your specific departments. That is your job, which I paid towards.

title: Lies about features : NO REFUND bc free trial period isn’t free
body:
It’s got pretty design but it wasn’t for me; they haven’t even bothered to check their shaky English.

The way most free trials work is you sign up; if you cancel before the end of the free period, you get your money back. 

I got suckered: I tried the app; it outright lied about its features; and it led me to believe I would be refunded if I cancelled within the trial period I would be refunded. Well, the fine print buries this, but guess what? Your free period ENDS WHEN YOU SUBSCRIBE. I’m screwed for $60. 

And they have TONS of fine print, including something saying you can only get a refund if you use the app for 20 days.  That’s illegal, at least in the US.

They LIED about having the MBTI test—doesn’t have it and all they have are some short clickbait ones. Avoid avoid!

title: Habit Tracker Could Use Some Work
body:
The app is cute and checking off tasks is fun. I even have the paid version of this app. But there are some major things lacking in the quality of life department that have me spending way too much time making and re-making my task list.

(1) You can’t edit tag names. You have to make a new tag, change each task over to the new tag, and then delete the old tag.
(2) You can’t mass-move tasks between tags. Opening up each task for editing and switching tags takes several clicks/taps and a surprising amount of time.
(3) You can set a specific time (8:00am) or a block of time (8:00am - 9:45am) for a task to be done in, but you can’t just say “morning” or “afternoon”. Setting an arbitrary exact start and stop time to define something like “morning” doesn’t feel good to my brain.
(4) If you don’t complete a weekly or monthly task on the exact day it’s set for, it doesn’t pop up until the next scheduled repeat. We really need an option to have non-completed tasks pop back up the next day. If I have a task titled “Laundry” set to repeat weekly on Mondays, and next Monday I fail to complete it, I need that uncompleted task to follow me into the next day. I will say you can go back in the calendar and retroactively complete a task, but you have to remember to do that, which is kind of counterproductive for this app’s goals.
Again, the app technically works as-is, but the setup is TIME CONSUMING, even with the ability to copy tasks. You pretty much need a game plan on how you want it organized when first going into it, because changing things afterwards is pretty painful.

title: Me + app review
body:
I’ve been using the Me+ app to help with my daily routines and honestly, it’s really helpful! The app lets you plan your morning, afternoon, and night routines in a cute and easy way. You can set little goals like brushing your teeth, drinking water, reading, or even doing skincare—and you check them off as you go.

The design is super aesthetic, with soft colors and a clean layout. It makes organizing your day feel fun, kind of like a game. One thing I really like is the little motivational quotes and fireworks when you complete your tasks—it makes you feel proud of yourself!

The only downside is that a lot of the good stuff is locked behind a paid plan, so if you don’t want to pay, you might feel limited. But even the free version is still pretty useful.

Overall:
If you want to get your life together, feel more organized, and build better habits (like waking up on time or doing homework), Me+ is a great app to try out!

title: Big Data Collection Tool that deprioritizes following a Schedule. Worse with each update
body:
I purchased this app and had quite a bit of success with it. As with all apps and social media you are trusting a corporation with your private data. Your schedule, your medications, your morning and night routines etc. 

When I first bought this app I accepted that but unfortunately with each update it keeps getting worse. (I am re-reviewing Me+ and yet again giving them 1star) They keep pushing terribly invasive new feature which you can’t click out of. The lasted terrible new feature is a “streak” window pops up every time you do your first task for the day. It doesn’t remember what you clicked the day before and you can’t close the window. It devalues the core purpose of the app which is to help you complete tasks. This standard way of pushing partial builds is absolutely the wrong way to improve this app. If the update frustrates me then it no longer helps me complete my tasks. They did the day idiotic update where they try to get you to record your mood when you open the app. It was implemented so poorly it made me want to stop using the app to check off items and stay on schedule. You had to actually had to close the entire App and start it again to avoid this. 

I’m not interested in this company knowing my mood, I did not purchase this for that reason and it is none of this corporation’s business what my “mood” is. 

The way this has been implemented it is clearly a data collection tool otherwise they would not try and force users to enter their mood. The way they have done things makes me want to stop using the app and more importantly makes it unnecessarily difficult to get to the screen where I can follow my routine checklist. 

I want my money back! 

Be warned this company is almost certainly selling your behavioral data even though it’s an App you have to pay for.  

Yet again gross corporate overstepping. This should be illegal. 

Notes on how to improve this App: 

1. Immediately fire your CEO for destroying your core product while trying to exploit your users 

2. Make a product that is actually beneficial for the users who pay for your product.

I contacted support (which btw isn’t easy to find on the app) after discovering I was charged $29.99 for three months. I THOUGHT I was signing up for a 7 days FREE  trial. Almost 72 hours and still NO responses from support. Charge though. I figure I would try it since hey, I’m being charge and likely not to be contacted. This has to be on of the worse apps I have ever seen for ADHD and organizing. The AI was good but then I go to add my own stuff and reset the entire thing. If you already know you brush your teeth, drink water, make your bed and take a walk save your money.

Just got a response from support. Here’s what it states: 

“Our product subscription….. ensuring you will NOT be charge for the free trial period”. 

3 reasons. But let me focus on #3 because NEVER EVER before have I got this on ANY OTHER app.
“Shorter sub. (Weekly, monthly, quarterly) also don’t include a free trial.” 

So congrats on finding a way to take advantage of people with ADHD while supposedly “helping” people with it. It’s full of cr-** . Download and lose money. But you will be reminded to brush your teeth. RUN away or get scammed. Look at all the critical reviews.

title: 2 years in and enjoying
body:
I started using this app to help me track my habits and  moods. This has been beneficial with helping aid in mental illness I was experiencing. I love that I can see my patterns and I now try to give myself grace during times where I know I need more rest. I have different hormonal imbalances that can make it challenging to create or even commit to a routine. This app has given me enjoyment in completing a task and how to be kind to myself when I don’t. It’s been easier to continue and try again with this app. I find it tedious to write and I’m always on my phone, so this app pairs well with my current habits. I love the daily affirmations and it even tracks your water intake. I now pay for the Me+ plan and it is a game changer. 

I started with their suggested task templates just to try getting into the habit of using this app. After a while I would make custom tasks that fit my comfort and goals. Again if you are someone who needs a little dopamine and serotonin high to help you commit to creating healthy habits  this is the app for you.  I would also recommend adding the widget that shows your entire daily task list in the phone to ensure it doesn’t become a lost thought.

title: Not meant for the neurospicy!
body:
This is just my personal opinion, so if you like the app, feel free to take my words with a grain of salt. Since I opened the app, it felt like it was made for neurotypical people. It’s very overstimulating. When you’re trying to explore the app, these ad-like pages pop up and to exit, you have to select “Give up feeling better.” I’ve never had an app try to guilt trip me? I’m just trying to explore the app.
The buttons bounce around and have blinking arrows pointing at them constantly so you can’t focus on reading about the routine. Also, none of the routines I’ve looked at seem practical for working professionals, and I can’t even open the built-in routines (the point of this app?) without a $19.99 pay wall, and no option for a free trial to see if it’s even worth giving them my money.
Also, it’s pretty overwhelming trying to explore all the options. Nothing is tailored to your needs through a questionnaire or something. Every tab on the app gives me more anxiety. It’s built more like a task list than a scheduled routine so again, not as useful as I hoped.
Everything about this app screams they have no idea how to appeal to a neurospicy brain. 

The only reason I gave this app 2 stars instead of 1 is because of the posts from healthcare professionals. There are some useful, interesting reads and videos from mental health and fitness professionals. Some of the printables are also useful but I wish they were customizable.

title: Love this app
body:
This is a great motivating app, I love how it has so many awesome options and helps you stay on track. It has sleeping care, reminders, smooth alarms, music, asks how your mood is to help with mental/physical health, and even small games to help get your mind working. There’s so much more but personally, those are my favorites, another thing I like about this app so far is that they suggest better help a super friendly and supportive therapy. 
If your life is turning into a mess, and you don’t know where or how to start then this would be a great app for you. Or if you forget you have to do something or feel unmotivated this app will help more than you suspect. 
I recommend this app a lot and hope you realize how much of a great experience this is.

title: a SAHM’s outlook
body:
I’ve been using Me+ for some time now, and I feel it helps me focus on the important tasks. I’m a SAHM, and I’m always eager to finish my daily housework list. However, I wish it didn’t ask how I’m doing or if I want to start my day every day. While I see the intention behind the “how I’m doing” question, I feel it should be an optional emotional gauge instead of a forced one. And of course, I’m ready to start my day– that’s why I’m logging into the app!

Also, sometimes I strive to set up the next day before it begins. But over the past year, I have noticed glitching when setting tasks for the following day. At times it’s too frustrating so I step away, missing out on valuable planning time or forgetting chores. PLEASE CORRECT THIS!!! Thank you in advance!

title: It’s ok
body: The app is cute and fun, but I noticed an issue. I create a repeating task. My schedule is always changing and every day can look different. So I need to change the times on some tasks, to accommodate for that day’s schedule. For example, I’d like to repeat the task “Make breakfast”… but it will not be at the same time very day. My schedule changes daily, weekly, and monthly. I recommend to anyone, to use Structured. That one is very easy to use. I wanted to try Me+ because of the other additions, like journaling, sleep aids, mood tracker, etc. That is a huge problem for me and I think I want my money back. I would spend WAY too much time “skipping” tasks and adding new ones at different times to accommodate my schedule. This should be easy to do with any app.

title: Looking forward to the meditation tab updates!!
body:
love this app! It’s really helped me stick to a routine, which has always been hard for me. It has everything you need to get started: workout videos, journaling for self-reflection, daily affirmations, mood tracking, and meditation. Plus, the yearly price is only $20, which is super reasonable. Honestly, I use it as an example of how apps like this should be priced—$10+ per month for some apps is just ridiculous when it’s already hard enough to build a routine!

My only complaint is with the recorded meditations. The guy’s voice is awful—he sounds like he’s giving a lecture, and it completely ruins the vibe. It’s a shame because he actually has the best meditation topics! I really hope they replace him with the female or add other voice options. Also, the meditation section is kind of limited, so I’d love to see them expand it.

title: Room for improvement but a great app
body:
I love this app. It makes me feel so productive and organized. However, there are some things that could use some work. 

Pros:
-the app is very customizable
-user-friendly and clear 
-love all the extra tools and resources provided 
- love that their is a option for subtasks 

Cons:
- although customizable, the apps color scheme seem limited to pastel colors. 
-target audience appears to be women based on schemes and resources 
-subtask list are fixed and are not able to be reordered 
-ai is a bit wonky when it comes to selecting photos from gallery 

Suggestions:
-create a community but allowing daily routine to be shared with friends/family 
-allow for the subtasks list to be reordered 
-add option for more color schemes rather than keeping things pastel

title: No Ability to Move Subtasks is a Dealbreaker
body: There is so much about this app that I appreciate. In fact, if it were not for this one particular issue, this would be my favorite app for Routines. However, the fact that there is no ability to move around and organize sub tasks within a task is a dealbreaker for me. I simply need that function because I like to consolidate subtasks in tasks, and I need the flexibility to change subtasks around on the fly. Developers, please add the ability to move subtasks by adding a standard push and drag function, so users can gain more control over subtasks! I will still use the app for a little while but it won’t be my go to, and when my subscription is up, I will have to look elsewhere unless this functionality is added, in which case, I’ll stay. Thanks

title: Cluttered app without free trial
body:
Th advertisements for this app are inaccurate. They say it is free. It is not. 

But I still wanted to try the free trial to see if this was an app that could help my ADHD son. As I was going through the sign up process to give it a trial to see what kind of function it would have for a teen guy, it asked if I wanted a discount. 

If you click “yes” your free trial is gone without warning. I went to cancel my 7 day free trial 5 days in only to find I was charged the full amount and that I have no trial. 

The app is unalterably feminine! 

As an adult female without ADHD, I still deleted the app even with a year’s paid subscription. So much clutter I can’t hide or remove is enough to make me not want to open the app!

title: Not worth the price
body:
Let's start with the good: This app is great for task planning and reminders. Sure, you can use the reminder apple app or google calendar for the same things but this is just a better & easier experience in the way that it's designed. Your UX designer needs a raise. 
Cons: This app is just not ready to be asking for a $15+ subscription. I would pay $5 at most for this. Unfortunately, I will not be re-subscribing. There are SO many issues and bugs. I am a software engineer and I notice a ton of bugs that are extremely disappointing for the price point. They absolutely did not do thorough testing. The most annoying one is that the app isn't compatible with CarPlay. For some reason it makes my audio sound like I'm recording and won't go away unless I close the app, at this point I don't even want to open it in the car at all--which is when I remember tasks I need to add.

title: Overwhelming without guidance
body:
As someone with AUDHD, this app is more like a Pinterest board of premade lists with cute graphics than a tool to actually help me figure out how to organize MY life. (Wash the curtains? Are you kidding?) Providing guidance for how to use the app would help instead of just throwing people into it. It seems made more for people who know what they want to do and want a fun way to write up their routines and get reminders for them than for people who struggle to create routines and need help. Also, it’s not true for people with ADHD that it takes 21 days to create a habit; revisit your neuroscience.

OH! And you baited and switched me! It said there was a 7 day free trial, then $59.99 a year. Then a pop up window said Thanksgiving special, the yearly subscription would be $29.99 instead. It was absolutely not clear that that negated the free trial, which is what I thought I was signing up for. That’s deceptive.

title: It’s great but needs improvements
body:
I love this app! I was recently diagnosed with ADHD and this has been incredibly helpful in creating great habits for myself. My home is cleaner than ever before and I rarely forget to do things if I remember to put it here. 

That said, I think there could still be a lot of improvements to make the app more functional. Below are the functions I would love to see split into what I see as “need-to-haves” vs “nice-to-haves”

Need to haves:

1) Create option to move “skipped” tasks to the bottom of checklist similar to “completed” tasks

2) Allow easier resorting under under “sort by time” without having to take multiple steps to change time OR standardize the way the manual sort list starts at the beginning of the day, as I have to resort the list in the order I want every day.

3) Allow us to choose where new “all day” tasks go in the list, rather than going to the top then having to drag and drop.

4) Allow us to make a one-time change to a recurring task (moving a task to another time or day outside of the recurring time, updating the sub task list, etc) without the change needing to apply to all future/past events. Similar to the options in google calendar events where it asks if the change is for this event or should apply to all future events.

5) Create an option for a task to happen within multiple days without having to pick a specific day. Example, if I have recurring task that need to happen sometime this week, but it doesn’t matter what day it happens on. 

6) Allow event editing after midnight. If i need to move something to another day and it’s past midnight my only option is to make a copy, instead of being able to move the item that already exists.

Nice to haves:

1) Number tasks and/or add a way to see how many tasks we have in a day, and how many are left. 

2) Add widget views within app experience. % completion, weekly checklist view, etc. 

3) Create an option to skip and rearrange subtasks

4) Add an option to move a task to tomorrow at the end of the day or next day move uncompleted tasks from the day before to today’s list. Allow us to review list to see if there is anything we don’t need to move.

5) Make task list items smaller or create a view all items view so it’s easier to drag and drop the order in manual sort

6) Add more emojis that correlate to common household chores (mopping, vacuuming, dusting, etc.) or household items (refrigerator, sink, table, coffee table, etc.). Maybe even remove some emojis that are repetitive.

title: Nice for some reminders but...
body: I set up this app as a way of keeping reminders around so that I don't procrastinate. I just want to be notified towards the end of the day I haven't finished one of the tasks yet.  However, if I turn notifications on, I'm constantly getting annoying little nudges that I need to check in more often, reminding me to give feedback about my mood, etc.  This sort of feedback should be optional. I don't really want a mood checker or self-affirmation of my emotional state, I just want a practical scheduler that consolidates my chore list and reminds me of the things I wrote in.  The other stuff is annoying to get notified of throughout the day, especially since I teach online and I turn notifications off for hundreds of my apps or else else I would constantly be getting these pop-ups.  People should have a choice of what they get, especially if they are bombarded with ads to upgrade, etc.  There also should be more ways of customizing times things need to be done, more customizable regular appointments (for example, every third week, or every three months, or every other day, etc.).  Plus, we should also get options to put off things for the next day (I realize that the point in the app is to not let us progress, but sometimes things are not practical to be done on a certain day… And I still want to be reminded that the chore does not go away (think it's one thing if we procrastinate subconsciously, but it's another thing when we actually consciously go in and change our schedules for outside reasons; that's not really procrastinating).  The other functions work fine and I like all the little icons and color coding.  The app has helped me stay organized and encouraged to stay on schedule, but the little notifications are so annoying that I may just go back to using the Apple calendar and checklists as reminders.

title: 4.5 stars, here’s why.
body: I’ve really enjoyed using Me+ for self-care, but there are a couple of areas where it could improve. For instance, when I take the tests, even if I only give one answer that might suggest feeling down or dealing with challenges, it categorizes me as “mildly depressed” or “abused.” This could be misleading or discouraging for users. One suggestion for enhancing the app would be adding a point system. With points, users could earn rewards for completing tasks, which would make sticking to goals more engaging. A small in-app game or shop where points could be used to “buy” fun items or upgrades would be a great incentive for consistency. Overall, Me+ is a great tool, but adding a few more features could really make it amazing!

title: I’m obsessed with this app!
body: I LOVE IT. What sets it apart from a regular  checklist is the widget feature, that I’ve expanded to take up one of my whole home screens. That way, it’s a gentle push to complete my daily activities, just by it being there. It’s too dang easy to ignore a checklist I have to open, or save, or write down. It’s right there every time I open my phone and I can’t forget or ignore it like I’ve done with All my other checklists. I also feel a great sense of satisfaction and pride at seeing the weekly stats of completion on each daily task. I haven’t gotten up on time or did my daily activities this consistently in a long time. I’m amazed something this simple actually works so well, just by it being there front and center on my phone. Try it, and try the widget feature! Also, start small and slow don’t add too many daily tasks or you might be tempted to just ignore it😂

title: Not helping me plan. Pushing its agenda.
body:
Don’t get this if you have anxiety or are looking for support setting routines. I thought this was going to help me. Instead it has increased my anxiety. 

All of the preset routines are ridiculous. Not things I can even begin to fathom as a starting point. Yeah, I can create my own, but there’s no guidance on best practices. 

Instead I keep getting “check in” - and then directed to tests (not scientific, share with friends, no suggestions on what to do based on results), therapy!!! and other apps by the creator. 

I purchased a year long subscription because it pushed me to “buy a year cheap” and then didn’t give me a free trial but charged me. 

Don’t

title: Tracking your progress is hard
body:
, so me+ should change the way how it counts the tasks ,or add a whole new system for tracking the tasks
I sort of enjoy this app but I have a problem on how it shows your progress, on the top where it says the days of the week the circle below ; it turns into a diamond when you complete all tasks , when you don’t it shows a silver star , which makes it harder to track your progress. To put into perspective imagine you complete 9/10 of tasks  on Monday it gives you a silver star ,on Tuesday you complete 10/10 of tasks the app gives you a diamond,on Wednesday you complete 3/10 of the tasks , it gives the same “rating” as the day you completed 9/10 of tasks even tho you did better on Monday so there’s no real way of tracking your progress and achievements.It would be very convenient for me+ to add a better system or various to better track your progress, and add a graph at the end of each month

title: The G.O.A.T. for productivity apps
body: I always try productivity apps, but rarely form a habit of using it on an ongoing basis and eventually forget about it.  I’m a fairly seasoned coder and considered just making an app for myself that had everything I needed in one place:  daily routine/schedule to help push through the adhd-ish procrastination, add recurring daily/weekly/monthly things like watering plants, and add one off to-do’s - with subtasks to keep me on target with the greater goal.  This app has all of that — and an absolutely gorgeous UI design, pop up reminders to keep me on track, and Home Screen widgets soon as I open my iPhone boom it’s there:  here’s what your day looks like.  This app is the most consistent I’ve ever been with using a productivity app, I’ve been absolutely slaying at my to do list, and it’s a pure treasure to my life.  Many thanks to the developers!

author: Lindy Looho

title: thank you, truly
body:
i have so honestly seen such a change in myself after using this. i understand that the things you have to pay money for are how the developers are profited, but for what you get for free i think is very generous and kind. im just a teen with no credit card, but if i wasn’t, i would definitely consider maximizing the usage of this app.

i think the set up and over all aesthetic this app provides makes you feel good and happy/excited to lay out your daily plan. i’m especially grateful for the alarm feature- the little “wake-up games” work incredibly well for me and i’ve gone from waking up at 11am-12pm (embarrassingly) to 7am. just those few hours make my day feel so much longer and more packed full of things to do.

i’ve been utilizing the sleep feature, and the reflection feature, and even been able to make physical improvements on myself using the workout feature, even if they are relatively easy workouts, having them there and at the ready makes me more likely to do them. 

i feel there’s so much more i have yet to discover, but of what ive been using so far i love it. i’ve limited my screen time, upped my productivity, and feel better mentally and physically. thank you so much, truly. i give my all to the developers!! ♥️

title: Just one thing
body:
Hello everyone. I want to give you a detailed explanation of how I feel about this app.

First I downloaded this in 2023 and I loved how free it was to use but I updated and it was heartbreaking to see that you removed my favorite thing about the app which was how you were able to pick from tasks instead of stressing yourself creating tasks to n your own. I understand that it is free to create your own tasks but allow us pick too.

I would also like to talk to you about the AI features of this app. 

I would love to experience the AI features of this app but make it limited at least. What I mean is make at least 30 chats per hour or day. The human chats and not the AI response.

Also I want the discover bar to be free to everyone. I want everyone to have tasks recommended but it says I have to pay which I do not like.

Overall, I really like this app and keep doing a great job understanding your users.

title: Useful and cute, but not for thorough planning
body: I use this app to check off my daily habits, and I occasionally add in something I need to do for that day. There is a lot of content that could be useful (meditations, mood tracker, sleep tracker, etc.), which I appreciate, but some of it I find a little unnecessary. This app is great for being more mindful about habits and the design is adorable and aesthetically pleasing, but I wouldn’t say it’s the most ideal for productivity, just because I find the layout a bit too close-up, if that makes sense. This has definitely helped me keep track of my daily and weekly habits, and I love so many things about it. I’m definitely gonna keep using this, and if you want to build new habits and feel accomplished, definitely try this app out. But if you’re looking to increase productivity and make to-do lists, I might suggest an actual planner. I love this app though!

title: So useful
body:
I downloaded a while ago but started using just recently and it’s incredibly helpful for remembering tasks I need to do. I used to keep track of it all on my notes app but it was very inefficient for me and this lets me make all those little weekly/daily tasks recurring so all I have to remember is to go on the app in the morning to tell me what I need to do. Seriously was a game changer for me, and is pretty affordable. I love you can customize any day whenever you remember. I was able to plan ahead for changes I knew would be coming in my life that would result in differences in routine. I read there were some restrictions on that/editing those in the past from some other reviews. Very glad they fixed it because it would’ve been useless to me otherwise. But because they did it’s fantastic.

UPDATE: Ok so it still won’t let you COMPLETE items ahead of time and it’s getting on my nerves. If I’m feeling super productive why shouldn’t I be able to get ahead? Especially if I have something coming up that means I won’t be able to do my tasks while I’m away?? Like I had to do them ahead of time then go back and fill them out on the day, which meant I had to remember which ones I’d done, which is one of the things this app is supposed to help me with! Very frustrating.

title: Great app! 😁
body: I love this app because it is good for visual people (or people who need a physical list) it also helps with people who tend to get distracted by other things around them. That was me. Organization is my #1 thing but I often had trouble just cleaning my room. I would find something while I was cleaning and start fiddling with it. But now that I download this app I really try my hardest to complete tasks. When you complete a task it sets off confetti BUT it also gives you a coin. I don’t think you can do anything with the coins but it makes me feel good! Another thing I like is that you can create a sub task. This is where if you create a task (clean bathroom) you can create a checklist for it (wipe down counters-fold towels-empty trash) it is great so you don’t forget what to do. If you allow the app to send you notifications it will send you reminders. There is one bedside to this: it will also send pointless notifications like how long it’s been since you last used the app. But anyway I hope I helped you! Have a good day! 😁

title: Please don’t promote yourself so aggressively
body:
I really like the idea of this app, and how it’s supposed to work. Combined calendar, to-do list, and mood tracker sounds incredibly helpful. 

I’m just put off by how aggressive this app is about trying to get people to buy. 
When I opened the app there was a long sequence of advertisements talking about how helpful the app is. And the setup quiz was mixed in so I couldn’t just skip. 
I didn’t even get to explore the app before it wanted me to buy a plan. And then when I started exploring, I got another ad for three other apps by the same company. 

All this feels really distracting in a productivity app. And it really lowered my mood when I had been having a good day so far.

title: Don’t be fooled by the try it free for 7 days.
body:
THEY WILL CHARGE YOU JUST FOR TRYING THE APP A MINIMUM OF ONE MONTH. Unfortunately I wasn’t savvy enough to catch it before they charged me $30.00.
First of all they are actually trying to sell you therapy sessions. I thought it would be an app that would help me get organized, as far as that goes it is only daily task lists. You can get the same thing from Pinterest for free. 
But the worst part of this app says  “free for 7 days.” Then to go on you have to choose between 3 different types of membership. But the 7 day free trial is not one of those choices, so I figured you just choose one and cancel before the 7 days are up. So I immediately went to my subscriptions and canceled it. I have done this many times before with other apps and there has never been a problem. Then I got an email saying a yearly subscription was billed to my Apple Card, and then it expired in 2025.  The whole thing is so misleading, from what it claims to be and the 7 days free. I don’t know if I have any recourse here or not but you can be sure I won’t use my Apple Card for anything being sold through the App Store. If I need to I will use a card that will take off any misleading or fraudulent charges.
This is the nail on the head in my decision to go with Samsung for my next phone.

title: ME+ App Review
body:
The ME+ app certainly has potential, and I appreciate its easy-to-use interface. It’s quite interactive, which adds to the overall experience. However, there is one major drawback: the ads to upgrade to the Pro version are very intrusive. They appear every time I open the app, which can be quite annoying.
I haven’t upgraded to the paid service yet because the app lacks some crucial features. The most important is the inability to add other people or use tags for tasks and notes. This is a major limitation for me, especially since there is another app available for free that offers these features along with similar functionalities.
While ME+ is more interactive and the team seems dedicated to improving the look and feel of the app, I think they should focus more on functionality. Adding the ability to tag other users in tasks and notes would be a game-changer for me. If this feature were available, I would definitely consider subscribing.
Consider these suggestions for future updates!

First, the frequency of a chore should be allowed to be marked for a certain weekday of each month. For example I’d like to clean my car in the 3rd Saturday of every month not just a particular date. Second I have been using the JustFit app, which led me to this app and vice versa. The problem is the 2 apps don’t link in any way so this app should automatically note that I completed a workout. And lastly, I would love to find an app that allows me to have the schedule tasks like this one does but then allow me to make an ongoing to-do list and be able to assign it to a day and time when it fit my schedule. I will likely not keep this app after my trial version as it feels like a basic task list with no bells and whistles.

title: SCAM
body:
Pay money: get more ads. This app is borderline predatory to those who are seeking help bettering themselves. Most of these reviews are from bots and your personal data isn’t secure once established. 

I got a year subscription but I keep getting ads the app for online therapy, a fitness app, a sleep tracker, and a food tracker that’s all owned by the same company. Why did I pay money to be told I need to download and buy more things?  Was my subscription not enough?

The additional services provided aren’t much better: take tests to see “the inner color of your true self “?   How is that going to help anything? What are you doing with all this data from these tests? 
The Discover tab does nothing but add the same routines from various charts that look like they’re been ripped off other pages with the watermark removed (reverse image search does wonders) to your daily list.  

It’s not doing anything to actually help, there’s nothing I’ve yet to find to promote better routines or fight executive dysfunction.

title: It’s really helpful
body: First of all, you can still do a lot of stuff without premium. Most of the premium options are good, but not necessary. Next, it has a lot of cool perks, like tests on ADHD, depression, and more. While they can’t really diagnose you, they give you tips based on your answers. (ie if you seem to have ADHD, it will give you daily tasks to keep you on task, like reminders to tidy up a bit daily.) Lastly, you can use your own input, you don’t have to pick from a list of things to do everyday. You can make your own and adjust, set reminders, alarms, and reputations based on what days you want to get them. There is so much more, but those are just a few things. If you want to get your life in order or need constant reminders like me, get this.

title: This app is a liar. Not for those who have ADHD
body:
This app. I am so so so angry and disappointed and frustrated by this app. It was advertised as being for people adhd to help them regulate and create good habits and then it ended up being by a glorified list maker that doesn’t even have proper templates for the lists?!?!? 

And it mockingly bothers you constantly about it. “How are you doing? How you feeling? Want to use one of our other apps that you also need to pay for to do some other task (probably poorly I would imagine) in your life?”

I have ADHD if I had the ability to create the routines and lists myself without being distracted I would just do it with calendar and the Notes app or a freaking to do list!! 

The whole point is app is to help me because that I can’t sort out activation and get overwhelmed with tasks. So giving me a blank slate in which to make up tasks becomes one more overwhelming thing I need to accomplish. 

This app is now part of the problem. And you made me PAY FOR IT BEFORE I could use it after telling me there was a free trial. 

So it’s just lies upon lies upon lies. Get bent, “Me”+. 

Anyone with ADHD (especially those with activation problems) looking for something to help, this ain’t it. Run.

author: Kitty Zee

title: Mixed feelings…
body:
I like the idea of the app: lots of tools in the box… but there are a few issues.

First, I installed the app just to poke around and see if it could be useful for me to help with time management  due to my ADHD. As soon as the app is installed, it starts pounding me with subscription and sales ads. Just as I’m about to click on the free trial so I can make a calm, informed decision about the app, a pop up sale for a year subscription with no free trial period takes over the screen and to make matters worse they give you 3 minutes to decide… which is kind of predatory when they market it for people like me who struggle with things like impulse control… so I succumb and give them my $30, without even getting to look at the app and its functionality…

Which brings me to my second issue, which comes down to how every time I look at the app I get sound hiccups and glitches. I love music, it’s played almost all day long on my device and every time I try to use the app to track my tasks as I cross them off my music is interrupted which is really jarring for me. 

Which brings me to my third issue; almost everything this app does can be done on as part of basic iOS apps. Tasks, alarms, calendars, reminders, and health all come standard. So now here I sit with an app that really only offers me some nature sounds and guided meditations both of which can be found free on YouTube or through Apple Music. I’m out $30 and I don’t see any reason to keep this app installed.

title: Make specific goals
body:
When I first got this app I wasn’t getting much out of it because my goals were too vague and lofty. They were too big to achieve easily. For example I had strength train before work. I accomplished the goal a few times but very little. I changed my goal to do 50 push ups a day and made 5 sub goals of 10 push ups throughout the day. This was much more realistic for my lifestyle and I really enjoyed checking off each set. The open ended time frame made it so I didn’t give up if I missed it, I could knock it out any time of day. This made a huge difference and I have since gotten a lot out of this app. 

This app isn’t magic, it’s 100% what you put into it. But it does have some great organizational features.

title: 🚨🚨🚨🚨SCAM ALERT🚨🚨🚨🚨
body:
Honestly, embarrassed that I fell for this. I should have read more reviews. 

They hook you in with a long quiz to get to know you (frankly I assume the app actually runs the same no matter the quiz results, but they will likely dispute that in their developer response) 

Then it gets to a payment page that says SEVEN DAY FREE TRIAL, but when a “GIFT” pops up offering HALF OFF and then starts a 3 minutes countdown to obviously pressure you buy, THEY FAIL TO DISCLOSE THAT YOU LOSE THE FREE TRIAL. 

Based on other reviews, I’m not even going to bother to go through their garbage customer service department and will instead go through Apple. 

They seem INCREDIBLY predatory and exploitative. 

Also, they push two of their other apps as well as routines in the app to “ help people lose weight” and “eat healthy” which is SUPER GROSS 🤢🤮 that’s literally how people develop eating disorders, and disordered relationships with their body, food, and exercise. 

People who are stressed out and looking for an app like this, and who are part of their target audience of having ADHD/being neurodivergent are already at a higher risk of developing eating disorders, and again this just seemed incredibly ill-informed, not remotely science backed, and predatory.

Even despite all of that I was shocked because they don’t even have that many routines available. 

OH and did I mention there’s in app content from TikTok users? Like idk how much they paid those people but ugh. So messed up. 

DO NOT DOWNLOAD. ITS NOT WORTH IT.

title: False advertising and instant charge!
body:
First, I was charged immediately for one year instead of getting the 7-day free trial. And reading the reviews now, it looks like I wasn’t the only one that was tricked into it with that 50% off offer (it wasn’t clear that choosing that offer meant not having a 7-day free trial).
Second, the app is not as advertised in the ads. The ads make it seem like the app breaks down large tasks like “pick up 10 items”, “put away all green items,” “gather all books,” but all the templates in the premium version are still so general like “do your laundry,” “make your bed,” etc. I went to the discord group that is supposed to be where to go to for support, and the people there just say something like “Everyone’s different, the templates are just there as a guide. You can create your own custom routine.” I struggle with ADHD, which is why the ad for this app appealed to me in the first place, because I need help with breaking down big tasks. I wouldn’t have paid for this app if I just have to make up my own routines anyways. I either want a refund or actual routine options like the one in advertised (not me having to make my own).

title: Not for teens
body:
Okay. So, I did let the subscription go through after the trial so that I can organize my life. But now that I’ve used it more, I will probably look for something else when the year is about up. The three stars are a combination of the good and the bad. The good is that it’s easy to set up recurring events and customize. But I feel concerned about some things. One, this app has a major agenda. It’s constantly asking me if I’m depressed and suggesting I take quizzes to see and every time I use it asking if I want to start online therapy with them. Wow, not even subtle. It also has a Pinterest/tiktock like page that features a curated mix of links such as “My life as a TikTok influencer.” What??? Is that supposed to be a role model for the same type of person who is depressed and needing therapy? There are also obvious grammatical errors that make me think the app’s made by someone which English as a second language, maybe someone in China since TikTok is so pushed. I would Never let a teenager or anyone at all impressionable use this app. In the meantime, I’m ignoring the constant pushing to start online therapy though it annoys me. 
Finally, if I “skip” a daily task, they should hide it or remove it from the list. Clearly, if I’m skipping it it’s because I’m trying to declutter my to do list for the day.

title: APP LACKS FLEXIBILITY
body:
Lots of “feel good” mood focus, and not enough flexibility. 

I completed a task a day early.  Tried to check it off, and the app just kept popping up with a “Let’s Focus on Today” banner.  The only way to check off the task was to change the date to the current day and then mark it complete.  The app seems to control my routine instead of giving me a tool to personally control my tasks as I wish.

Also, I wanted to set a recurring reminder for a specific task for several different times throughout a single day.  As far as I could see there is no way to do this.  Contacted developers, the only way available, feedback within the app, but no response after 2 weeks.

I could also do without the silly animated stuff and juvenile, caricature-like feel of this app.  

Requested a refund through the App Store since the app does not work as described.  This app makes keeping track of my daily routine a hassle, and cumbersome at best.

title: helpful but misleading
body: I just got this app and I am genuinely enjoying it and have found it helpful thus far, however, I joined Me+ under the impression that I had a 7 day long free trial and THEN was to be charged $12.99 + tax once the 7 days were up. Incorrect. I was charged $14.17 immediately after signing up for the free trial so now I have a month of this subscription that I didn’t want to begin with. It’s unfortunate that such an awesome app is so misleading with their advertising. If you don’t actually offer a 7 day free trial, why say you do? Anyways, if you’re looking for a $14.17 per month subscription that helps with ADHD related struggles, this app is definitely suitable for you. One upside is that I’ve noticed the app does help me with my bipolar when I have down days, so I can actually get at least one thing off my list. 
Overall, I will give the me+ app 3 stars because while it does have some benefits for people with bipolar or adhd, the loss of the templates makes the app less effective and harder to use. I’ll beg y’all or pay y’all money to add the templates back please 😭

Unfortunately, the terms & conditions weren’t mobile friendly either.

title: Useful but could be better
body: First of all, it collects too much data. Secondly, It generates some cleaning lists but it's not in depth and contains duplicate items. If I just followed the list, there would be many areas in the house that never got touched at all. It seems like an ok app for someone living alone in an apartment but entirely insufficient for a family with young kids in a house. Third, It's also full of grammatical errors ("Laundry the dish cloths") and needs to be proof read. Fourth, it has too many ads popping up asking me to download their other apps. Fifth, the exercise task list doesn't take into account your fitness level. Their list to achieve an "ideal body" is aimed at women who want to be influencers, I think? It proclaims it will give you a big bust, small waist, big butt, and thick thighs. I'm not trying to disparage the aesthetic but my ideal body has a strong core, flexible joints, and a healthy heart. Which brings me to my last point: it seems to be related to TikTok somehow because many items in the library are "a day in the life of a TikTok influencer." I downloaded the app for the Spring Cleaning challenge thinking that it would give me a to-do list to get me started, but it just asked me to make videos about cleaning, post them to TikTok, and tag them for the chance to win a prize. I'm trying to clean and organize my whole house from basement to attic and this is not helpful.

title: Encouraging Accountability
body:
I had about a 6.5 year depression. I’ve been out of it for a couple of years but I wasn’t making progress with my home and health and I was scared I’d relapse after my youngest child was born. I’ve heard a lot about this app so I tried it and I’m thrilled. I set timers and it reminds me to not stay out late and come home to do my end of the night things.

This motivates me in the morning to do my morning things. Having the tags and color coded really helps me. I made a tag for baby things and it helps me to get things done every day so I don’t get overwhelmed. Another great thing is the sounds and meditation. When my 6 wk old is needed me to hold him and I want to get things done I sit and rock him and play the rainforest sounds. He falls asleep and I get relaxed. Then I can resume my tasks in peace. Truly I’m enjoying this postpartum time and I didn’t know if I would. This app is helpful in keeping me accountable in an encouraging way.

title: The audacity
body: This app goes through a billion superficial questions that have you click the same continue button in between little animations patting itself on the back for how great it is. It felt like 1000 versions of the same “we’re great, don’t you want to be great too?” type question. Then it asks for a subscription fee afterwards and it isn’t cheap. The audacity to run people through the monotonous process of clicking a single button over and over again while gloating about how helpful and wonderful your app is, and then saying “oh but you can’t have any of that benefit unless you pay” is disgusting. Isn’t the time and energy for a person with adhd trying to organize themselves enough to ask? Isn’t the desire to solve chronic issues that cause problems in a persons life enough of a reason to be able to make said change happen? No? You have to ask for money? Mental struggle isn’t good enough for you, you want more? You have to contribute to financial struggle as well? And you can’t even be up front about it! So gross. On the App Store it’s marketed as a free app with in-app-purchases. That doesn’t count if the only free part I can use is the subscription options menu. I didn’t even get a chance to use this app so maybe people who are okay wasting money can say it works fine but personally I have enough to deal with and essential stuff is already expensive enough that I can’t justify a subscription for this. I hate living in a world where even things made to be helpful for those in need are designed to nickel and dime the user. Your app made my life worse just with my minutes-long interaction with it. The only real piece of critique I can give through all my layers of frustration is that you should be explicit about the need to pay. Just have the first window ask for a subscription like every other stanky money grubbing app does, don’t drag a user through a process of watching you brag about how great you are and then throw it back in their face by saying that the user must pay.

title: Charged without 7 day trial, mediocre app
body:
So I downloaded this app and it said I’d get a free trial, but it charged me automatically after signing up. I thought whatever I’ll just use it I guess. I tried to make a routine and it was fine but I have kind of weird hours at my job and if I didn’t check off everything it would just tell me to make my routines shorter down to the point where it was just to drink water and like take my pills. Which wasn’t really helping me be productive like the app is advertised for. It’s also extremely easy to ignore the notifications, there’s nothing that makes you want to get stuff done besides the reminders. I’m really trying to discipline myself after going thru some of the worst anxiety and adhd paralysis I’ve had in a while and this app definitely wasn’t helpful. 

It also has options where you could record how you feel each day, things to help you write out why your anxious/sad/angry/etc that are supposed to help you work through your emotions but it wasn’t super helpful for me at all. I think everything this app has could be achieved through a quick Google search of exercising how to stay on task and keeping a list on your phones notepad to write down your daily tasks and how your feeling. 

One thing I thought was cool at first was the sleep tracker, something I always wanted to try, but the only thing it picked up sound wise was the simpsons on my tv (played extremely low), and it only picked up when Lenny was talking which was kind of weird. It also picked up my boyfriends sleep sounds, none of mine tho. That’s my bad, but I just kind of expected it to pick up only the sounds that were directly next to the sound (me).

Overall I think this app could help someone maybe more organized and determined than I. I think you already need to be in a routine mindset. As a 20 something year old tattoo artist who works 12 hours a day, it wasn’t super helpful. I think if there was an option to discipline the person using it, like locking the phone until a task is done (idk if that is possible tho) then maybe it would be worth the $30 a year. This right now is something that I can do for free and think it would honestly be more helpful to organize a list and tasks myself. 

Hope this helps anyone who reads it! The TikTok and Instagram ads aren’t always the best at showing you what the app is really about and really glorifies it as a fix-all for your problems.

title: BEWARE Falsely advertised app. you do NOT get a 7-day subscription.
body: I never write reviews, but for this app, I wish I filtered the reviews from the most critical. Please do not get this app. When filling out the test, it gives you a subscription prompt . a monthly and yearly subscription. with the yearly you get a seven day free trial, so I selected that to see if I will actually like the app. And before finalizing the payment, the app gave me a 50% off coupon for the year.(I did not have the option to decline the 50% off) I did not want to pay for the year, but it advertises that I still will have my seven day trial so I went with it. I didn’t know it will actually charge me the same day. And when looking back, I saw no advertisement that I will be charged immediately once selecting the yearly sub. after going through the reviews, I saw the app give out their email and I reached out to customer service(which is awful) they tell me that because I had a yearly discount I was unable to do the seven day free trial, which again was not advertised. They are very rude and that is why I’m also leaving a star review. PLEASE SAVE YOUR MONEY AND DO NOT GET THIS APP. title: Good App.. But has some issues
body:
Overall I think this is a great app, it’s easy and simple. Whether you want a rigid day to day fully remind task oriented day, or just need to remember a few things it’s genuinely great. 
   Pros:
1. you can add tasks indavidually or have them repeat daily, weekly or monthly.
2. You can have reminders and even pre-reminders on each task
3. You get to name each task, assign a color and an emoji
4. There are sub tasks within each tasks as well as tags for grouping all of the same things. I.E. you want to only see all your workout tasks or doctor appoints etc.
5. You can widgets for other apps in it.
6. It’s easy to use and understand and the price really is a great selling point.

Cons:
1. You can only add tasks either individually or daily or weekly or monthly. So if you have a repeat task (running 3x a week) you have to either type that task in 3 times each week or you have go in and skip every day you don’t want to do that task.
2. You cannot copy and past tasks. It would be great to have the ability to copy the tasks to other days, or be able to edit the on to specific days. So I want to work out Monday, Wednesday and Friday: you either have to add it to repeat daily and go back trough every day and skip that you don’t want to use it or you have to type that same task over and over every time you want to do it. (which if this is on going is extremely time consuming and can be overwhelming) a copy and paste or ability to edit different days would be great.
3. If a task isn’t completed that’s it’s, there no option remind you to change it or move it. It’s that day or nothing. A remind to keep on the task would be great for things that aren’t daily like if I need to grocery shop and I set for Tuesday but run out of time. You have to remember to go in or change it or retype to another day. 
4. More of a nit picky - thing but a few more useful emojis would be nice and more colors would be great. Also the type to generate is horrible I typed in water and it gave me something weird. Also walk my dog gave me just a man walking. Emojis like a water bottle for water reminders, etc but with the search function to match would be nice but not really a big deal. 

Again over all great app and idea I like it and use it but a few things changed would make it much better and would warrant more then 3 stars. Hopefully we can see some updates with these kind of things and even more! It would be nice to see more features and options.

title: No idea how this has 4.8 stars…
body:
This app must have bot reviews; it’s incomplete, riddled with bad grammar, and missing basic and obvious features. 

- There’s no cloud backup of data
- The widgets are half-baked, and don’t update when you cross items off
- The cost ($40/yr at time of writing) is extreme for the feature set (or lack thereof)
- Reminders come up even if the task is already crossed off
- Task ordering makes no sense
- There’s some questions when you start the app. They have zero effect on what the app does, it’s just collecting your data because it can. 
- The app keeps advertising itself in barely-subtle ways, trying much harder to convince you it’s doing a good job than it tries to do a good job. 

Overall, waste of time. Look for alternatives.

body:
Update: if you manually add a task there is a weekly option so that’s good but why wasn’t that an option when adding from the premade lists?

There’s a 7 day free trial but if you choose the discount price you get charged right away which was a surprise. Since I’ve inadvertently already paid for the year, I will put some things on my list and give it a try. Who knows maybe I’ll find it useful

title: Helps me get things done
body:
I don’t like cleaning as a rule 🤷‍♀️ I get overwhelmed by “all the things” that have to get done, I’m like “oh there’s my bed” or “I’ll just play one game on my iPad”. 6 hours later nothing is done.

But with this app I’m getting things done every day. I chose the one for chores, I can determine how often they get done. I added specific things to my household. It feels good to check off an item and when I check off all the items for that day a little ding happens with confetti- it’s a little dopamine hit. 

The app is cute and I just started in the library for meditations so it has a lot to offer. I recommend it if you have ADD or anxiety or just overwhelmed my the mundane tasks.  I’ve only had it for a week but I’m really enjoying checking off those mundane tasks.

title: “Free” Trial Immediately Charged Me $32.09
body:
As far as I can remember, I’ve never left a review for an app, but I had to warn my fellow consumers, especially those who are downloading this app in an effort to better themselves.

I was terribly mislead. I signed up for their “free” trial just to LOOK at the app and was IMMEDIATELY charged $32.09. 

I downloaded several similar apps just to see which I wanted to commit to. Even despite now having access to all Me+ has to offer, I plan to use Habit. It allows you to set multiple notifications per day for different times of the day, share your “habits”/goals and progress with your friends so that they can help by holding you accountable and offering their support, in my personal opinion it’s significantly more aesthetically pleasing and user friendly, and GET THIS, you can set up to 5 “habits” for free or you can pay a ONE TIME (EVER) FEE of $9 to gain full access. LOVE IT!

title: Used to be great but new update made it way worse
body:
Been using this app for about 6 months. Used to be great and you could track individual task and it would let you know your streaks and give you data on habits.

Right now the data doesn’t track your streaks or anything aside from times completed when you look at specific tasks, and on top of that the old UI with the pretty medals showing your completion streaks and data are all gone. So if you want to see your progress over time for individual tasks you basically get nothing, which defeats the purpose. 

Currently they’ve also removed a ton of functionality from the tasks checklist (tasks can no longer have multiple checks before completion ie: instead of having to drink water 6 times for completion and being able to track each time you drink water, it’s now just “drink water” either finished or not finished, which makes tracking tasks that are ongoing way worse. 

I’ve sent them an email about this but no response and I do feel as if the app’s not really being worked on much anymore. Just seems like the app is progressively becoming more barebones, compared to apps with active teams that are constantly adding features or improving things. Would not recommend if you’re looking for a long term app as it’s likely to get even worse tbh. Used to be great though! Good luck in your habit app search!

title: Only lists and false advertising
body: I was looking for an app to help my teen with organization and read about this app on a couple of websites. I downloaded it to check it out, but could not access any features without a “free 2-week trial”. I decided to try it. It was pretty disappointing because it seemed there were nothing but lists — choose things you want to change or choose habits you want to increase — which only created an extremely long “to do” list that would seem to overwhelm anyone! I knew this was not what I was looking for and within an hour cancelled the subscription and deleted the app. I checked the status in my subscriptions for the next two week to be sure I had cancelled and wouldn’t be charged. However, I was still charged for a yearly subscription — even though my subscription list in my account said it was cancelled. I had to request a refund through Apple and I was able to get my money back, but this app is not worth it to trying for all the hassle of chasing down your a refund.

title: It’s good but also disappointing
body:
I was very excited for this app because I’ve been looking for something to help me manage my day. I love the tips and the designs and little helps, but when it comes to actual functionality, it falls very short.
For example, when they offer you exercises to do with great visuals and instructions, they offer you a task to put on your calendar to do that exercise every day. The task ONLY has the exercise name. No description or Instructions or even images of what the exercise looks like. The least they could provide is a link to it.  I have to go look up the exercise to complete the task, but it’s not easy to find because it was in a little helpful hint video kinda thing. And maybe I watched 4 videos and added 10 tasks… I have no idea where to find that specific exercise. I could SS, but then i can’t even add a SS to the task.
Also, if you add a task to your day and don’t complete it, it doesn’t carry over to the next day. So if I wake up and want to know what tasks I have missed the last few days, I have to scroll through each day. I can then copy the task to today, but what a PITA. There is literally NO task management functionality. 
They have the beginnings of a great product here, but there’s still a long way to go. Hopefully they’re using the $$ they charged me to invest in development.

title: Life changer for routines!
body:
As a sophomore and very messy girl, I find it awfully hard to have a routine, let alone be consistent. But I decided after saying year after year “I’ll be different and reach my goals more efficiently “ . But I had no where to even start. I saw ads about me+ and I was skeptical at first, so 2 weeks ago I decided to try it out. 

I tested myself on their ADHD test, and I was likely to have adhd, but that’s not the point. This app actually helps me get things done and It doesn’t feel like a forced routine! I actually feel like I can have somewhat consistency and organization, I get reminded to do stuff, and remember to do them! The format of their tasks is so easy to understand, and I actually developed a workout routine with this app! I plan to more stuff, and this app offers reflection, check-ins, and much more! I use the free version, and I think that’ll be enough for me. I ADORE the fact that this planner app doesn’t shove ads on your face. I honestly feel like I’ve found the planner to actually help me organize myself : )

Even worse is that the app sends me push notifications about being on “thin ice” because I’m supposedly not completing my New Year’s resolution task each day, when in fact I am, it’s just not being recorded because of a bug in your app. Very annoying.

title: Me+review and some questions
body:
I just got this app and love it! I have only used it for one day and already feel more organized and confident!

Every thing is amazing!

There is two thing I wish would be different at least in my opinion. 

1. I haven’t tested the workouts yet but by the looks there aren’t that many and I’m the type of person who likes to have one app for multiple things. title: Deceptive and manipulative
body:
From other reviews, I was led to believe this is a free app. It’s not. 

When you first open it up, it takes you along a marketing journey filled with self-congratulatory language, stats without sources, and a bunch of misspellings (“recoreded” and “ADHA”? Really?). 

Then it forces you to pay money to use the app, pretending like you miraculously won 50% off the annual subscription. 

Awful. I really needed an app like this as a neurodivergent person, but this is done so poorly from the get-go that it’s just disappointing. Time to find a better app.

title: Love it!
body:
So let me start off by saying that I’m really enjoying this app. Setting up a daily schedule is fairly simple. They give you a few suggested things to do or different routines or you can make up your own tasks and time schedule. I also love the Reflection page and working on those writing prompts. Definitely would like to see more of those down the road.

Things I don’t like or don’t work; Alarms, they don’t go off at all. Reminders never go off either and my settings allow for notifications from the app. So getting those two to work would be amazing.
On the daily list schedule I wish there was a way to sort everything by time so I don’t have to go through each individual task and sort it to the appropriate area on the list. I also wish there was a day view/week view with a total task count on each day so you’ll be able to look at your week as a whole to see which days have more or less things planned instead of having to go in day by day to get an idea of what’s there.
For tasks: Let’s face it, we plan a day and are not able to get to everything we want to in a day because life happens. I wish daily tasks had a skip or postpone option for just the day where hitting that option would move that task to the next day but keep the original schedule going. Right now it appears I’d have to go into the task to change it and sometimes I don’t have that much time to fiddle with the app..

Those are just some thoughts and I’m sure there will be more! But so far so good with the app and I’m excited to hopefully see this grow into a powerhouse that really helps people who are struggling with making/keeping a routine or just need little nudges through the day.
