title: HATE THE NEW UPDATE
body:
Every day since I downloaded this app and became a paying member I’ve wondered what the $40 is for. Most of the stuff advertised has never worked and the new update completely ruined what little I did like about this app. 

I can’t update any of my tasks, change the icon, edit subtasks, add reminders, or change the order they are in. It advertises that you can adjust your schedule by the time of day but you absolutely cannot, the only option is to add a reminder time but it doesn’t change where it’s located in your routine. If you do the manual labor to drag everything where you do want it, it’s only for that day and all future days are in the random order again. You can only “tag” your morning/evening routines, they don’t actually create a morning or evening routine, no idea what the tags are for honestly. 

Prior to the update I had tasks that I completed several times throughout the day (drinking water, washing my face, etc.) and it had the option to hit “complete” after doing each individual task but after the update they took that out and you only have the option to add subtasks, which for me are not helpful, and only one time to actually complete the task. 

Another big complaint I’ve had since the beginning is that I have weekly/monthly tasks that I only need to complete one time throughout the week/month but there is so way to create a task list outside of a daily one. You have to assign days to complete the tasks on, but I don’t always know what day of the month I’ll have time to do that task. There should be a weekly/monthly section along with the daily to better organize larger tasks. 

I had a lot of hope for this app as someone who struggles with ADHD but I’ve been consistently disappointed and will certainly not be renewing my membership.

title: Double billed & Ignoring my request for refund
body:
I signed up for the ME+ scheduling app. on August 4, 2023 and while reconciling my account I found that I had been charged twice for this subscription. The first charge was $21.71 (a $19.99 special offer) and the second charge was $43.43 ($39.99 Me+ VIP) for an annual membership. 

What I believe happened is that I attempted to subscribe for one plan and my credit card had expired so it did not immediately process, so I went back to my apple/itunes settings and updated my credit card information. When I returned to the Me+ app. to complete my subscription sign-up, it had a pop-up special offer that was less expensive, so I selected that option. Then when the apple system updated and attempted to recharge my credit card for the original selection, it went through and was processed. So I was charged for both subscriptions. 

I have requested a refund THREE TIMES and received a response that you received it and will get back to me, but you never did. If you had refunded one of the subscriptions I might have been a repeat customer - but because you charged me twice and refuse to refund me, I am led to believe you are conducting fraudulent practices. I will start here with my negative review then I will actively promote my dissatisfaction on every social media platform I have, file with the BBB, and other legal remedies. I currently have 10.7k followers on just one account. 

Double charges happen, mistakes happen, but it is your refusal to refund the double charges that makes your business practice fraudulent and people should be warned.

title: I like it - but some enhancements can help
body:
I like the look and feel of the app. No complaints so far. 

I just started using it today and I noticed that there are some things that could help with usability. 

1- changing the emoji related to the task is annoying because there isn’t a way to filter the emojis by category or search by name. I have to scroll through a long list and sometimes it’s difficult to find what I’m looking for. 

2 - for weekly or monthly tasks that repeat, I would like the ability to move them to a different date. Example: if I have a reminder for a “spa night” every Friday but for some reason I’m not able to do it this week and I want to change it to Saturday I have to skip the entire task and then recreate it for a new day or else it shifts all the future tasks in my schedule.

body:
See I first downloaded this app due to the fact I have ADHD so I would forget a lot, this app helped me through it tremendously and every time i would forget i would get a notification that would be sent to my phone with a sweet little motivation note. Im so grateful for this app indeed.

You see I left to go overseas on a vacation with family but i go back to the app the week later and find out the style change. I find the bird or goose or whatever the funk that creature is. Back to the point I hate the app change it makes the app so lame now and now every time I go to check off something i completed its like all that bubbly stuff makes it harder for me to actually WANT to do it. Im sorry for this little rant honestly. Its not to come attack you or anything I just feel like i need to express my opinion. 

Thank You Have a Nice Day.

title: Garbage and scammy
body:
I would highly recommend not getting this app. 

This app looks pretty and all the wording is upbeat, but the grammar is absolutely atrocious throughout. 

It’s either AI generated text and no one is editing, or it’s translated from another language… and no one is editing. 

Also it claims to give you a 7 day free trial, but then charges you right away. When you go to the questions page about subscriptions, it gives you a false link that doesn’t go anywhere. 

There is very limited information on your profile page, so you have no info and no control over your subscription within the app itself. 

This app also pushes TikTok influencers… which is weird and irrelevant to being more organized and keeping routines. 

The whole thing is weird and I’m NOT HAPPY that I had money taken from my account without my permission.

title: This app is weird
body: It’s an ok app overall, but there are some things I’d like to point out that I don’t see anyone talking about. In some of these plans, there are ones that depict simply unrealistic lifestyles in general. One of these being “a realistic morning routine starts at 4:30 am”. I’m also not a fan of a lot of these graphics. In the healthy lifestyle section specifically. They mostly depict women who are overweight and sad, then become skinny and are magically happy. Let me start with saying that being skinny isn’t the key to happiness. And that these are unrealistic results for a 30 day plan. If you got this far, thank you. I’m not completely bashing the idea of this app, I’m bashing the idea that happiness comes from skinniness, and that anyone ( that I know at least) is gonna wake up at 4:30 in the morning for a whole routine. Thank you again for listening.

title: NO NO NO why did you change it 😩
body: As an AuDHDer change is really difficult for me. I understand app updates but the icons aren’t streamlined looking anymore and my huge issue is that in the older version, when you completed a task it was bumped to the bottom of the list. This is HUGE for people with object permanence issues because is moves the thing we already did out of the way and puts the things we haven’t done in front of us where we don’t have to scroll to see it. This for me was the big reason I paid for a yearly subscription for the app. A physical to do list cannot bump itself and center my unfinished tasks. Please change this back, I know I can’t be the only one who feels this way. As someone who has used this app everyday for 5 months and has been greatly helped by it, this one seemingly small thing might kill the whole app for me.

title: For young girls
body:
As a grown woman, i couldn’t completely relate to the app. The diagrams, messaging, templates all hint towards young girls who are learning about themselves and working to build healthy habits. 

The reminders were rigid and not robust, meaning it’s an ‘either/or’ situation when it comes to setting up and categorizing the reminders. 

You can’t search the icons to add to the reminders, and again the icons were geared towards the youth. 

The app refers you to other apps that also have fees attached to them. 

I think the worst thing was that that’s no way to log into this app on other devices, you have to set it up all over again on that device. 

It’s too manual and not AI driven. 

I think this app is great for beginners who don’t require too much and just want to get started somewhere.

title: Good app
body: I just got this app yesterday and I already love it! I really wanted to improve my body and health for the new year. With this app you can track your goals and make a list of them to complete daily, weekly, and monthly. Every day my goal is to drink at least 6 glasses of water to stay hydrated and after I accomplished my goal I would check it off. By checking my goals off it really motivates me to keep going and adding to my list because it makes me feel successful. You can also record how you feel for the day and explore self care plans that you can add to your list. What I also love about this app is if your struggling with something in your life you take a survey about it and it will give you ideas on how to solve a problem. This app includes 5-10 minute meditation sessions and workouts for your body! A fun detail I loved about this app is being able to color coordinate all tasks on your to do list. Overall this apps really helps to improve my health, be more active and productive, and best be a better version of myself. Thanks!

title: Overrated
body:
I was super excited for this. It sounded like it was going to be a more detailed, CBT driven program, not just a to-do list. It had me take this “assessment” and seemed like it would forumulate a more custom process with goals. What I got was 1 item on my list: “stand and gaze time”.  That was the only item it added. The rest I could either add myself or go into their “library”. Some of them were things like, “Clean my room”. Who with ADHD hasn’t made 100 lists over their lifetime with items like, “Clean my room”, “Do the dishes”. If that worked we wouldn’t be here.
Alternatively you can choose from not a ton of pre-made templates that also give very little insight. (You can also search through influencers that talk about the app. Yay! 🙄) Most of this seems like marketing for their other apps.
Sure, the esthetic is great. But this is really just an over-priced to-do list. You reminders app in iOS does the same thing and it’s free.

title: Mixed feelings
body: I started using this app and have mixed feelings about it. Since using this app, I have definitely built a system and I do feel like I get things done. HOWEVER, it is basically a fancy looking reminders list… if you have an iPhone or iPad it comes with a reminder app that basically does the exact same thing, it’s just less aesthetic. Me+ and the reminder app both have a task list and then a little circle to check it off. I would seriously save your money if you just want to schedule out your day and tasks. Another thing that bothers me about this app is the order of your tasks NEVER STAYS THE SAME. I like to have my tasks in the order I want to get them done, but everyday that I log in they rearrange the order EVERY TIME. This makes me so frustrated because it takes me forever to reorganize them in the right order. I feel like this app is wayyyyyy overpriced for what it is. In fact, this app should be free. They do have built in routines which I guess is cool, but you can literally find thousands of routines on Pinterest for free. You could literally copy them in your reminder app and get the same result. In conclusion, if buying this app will keep you more accountable, then by all means, buy it. But if you are just looking for something to keep your task list in order, use the FREE apple reminder app and your calendar! I definitely feel like buying this app was a waste for me.

title: Disappointing
body:
Had high hopes for this app but it was very disappointing. First I fought I was signing up for a trial but it turns out they charged me for a year (I’m fine with paying but the prices said FREE TRIAL and when I initially declined it offered reduced rates which did not include a trial period.) 

Wasn’t a big fan of the interface or flow; it just didn’t work for me, if the tasks could be sequenced better, given specific times or maybe even quadrants of the day it might have been more helpful. For me it was just more frustrating than helpful might not be that way for everyone, in fact it probably isn’t. 

Biggest annoyance was despite the fact I paid for an entire year I kept getting bombarded with ads for other apps just really distracting and off putting. Every time I completed a task another screen popped up pushing other apps. If these aren’t ads for other products this probably needs to be explained better. Also I should be able to opt out of seeing this seemingly every time I complete a task. 

While it didn’t work for me I can see how this could be helpful to a lot of people. I have very particular ways of dealing with tasks and just because it didn’t work for me doesn’t mean it’s not going to work for you.

I don’t appreciate apps that make scientific claims but in reality are not scientifically based - it’s deceitful and dishonest. I recommend you explore other options.

title: Bugs need to be fixed
body:
I like this app but there are a couple of bugs and suggestions I have.

1) When I add a new routine it doesn’t show up. I added drink water and it didn’t show up so I added it again and about a day later they both showed up. Now 2 that were missing showed up and all the other ones disappeared. It would be great if this could be fixed because I like this app but currently can’t use it and from what I’ve read I’m not the only one with this problem. 

 2) it would be great if when you click in a routine it could show up with one of the things on your checklist at a time. I’ve seen other apps that do this where you start a routine and it goes through each task on your list one at a time and I’d love if you could do that with this app. 

 3) lastly it would be great if some of the more basic pre made routines were free because sometimes making your own is hard so maybe you could create a few free ones like a morning and night routine. 

4) When you make a routine for specific days you can only edit them on those days which is very annoying especially if you make a mistake in which days you want it on.

I’d love if all of these were fixed but the most important are the first and last.  Please fix it because I like this app. Thank you for your time!

title: SUBSCRIPTION BASED
body:
I had a creeping feeling that this app wasn’t really free when it opened by trying to convince you of how great and effective it is. And it does this for many screens, while also asking you questions about your mental health and assuring you that it could, in a sense, cure you.

 All of this, just to bring you to a subscription paywall. Even with a free trial, that’s low to the desperate people in need. You know that if they take the free trial, and it works for them, it becomes an impossible service to live without. 

But being honest, no one should have to pay MONTHLY for a schedule planner. I understand that developers need payment, and I would be genuinely happy with a one time payment to this app, even if it’s sort of expensive, but this isn’t what you’ve done. I don’t care how psychologically backed up your methods are, all one of these apps really needs is intuitive/custom scheduling methods and a bit of confetti, which I haven’t been able to find in a single IOS planner app without first running into a subscription paywall. What a shame.

title: Worth the $29.99 a year!
body: I struggle with getting my daily tasks done having ADHD. I've tried at least 10 task apps that were worthless or obscenely expensive for the little they did. I tried this app after searching for a task app specifically for people like me with ADHD. After setting up all the tasks on this app that I had set up on my previous task app, I did my first day already and looked forward to getting them all done. It gives me the right hit of dopamine to keep me coming back and using it. If you're on the fence? Don't be! It gives you a free seven-day trial, and I didn't need it to know it was the right app for me. I paid for an entire year, and after only using it for 2 hours, I knew I made the right choice. $29.99 for 12 months? That's a steal today!

title: AMAZING! But…
body: First off let me just say, I have severe ADHD. I never plan stuff, always get off task/distracted, and I’m always on my phone. When I was scrolling though YT I saw an add and thought “maybe this will help me become a better person!” I hesitated a first for a while but finally decided that I was gonna try it out. The serve they make u take in the beginning is amazing! I don’t care if it’s long it’s awesome. Overall this is an amazing app and helped me reduce my screen time, get on track, and not get distracted. But… the only things are when I try to make my own reminder thing, like let’s say a b-day party. You don’t have a b-day party every day so I just wanted it on a certain day. Well when I tried to do that it kept adding it to today instead of the day I wanted. So it took me 10 minutes trying to figure out what to do. And the other thing is I wish we could just pick an emoji from our keyboard instead of the recommended icons. That’s it all I think is just fix a few things and bugs. Totally recommend and have a good day!

title: PLEASE FIX THIS
body:
This app is amazing. I love how it’s color coded and how I can easily rearrange my tasks for the day. I also love how it tracks your habits as it holds me accountable to complete them. However, as someone with ADHD and anxiety, there are a few things that bother me that I wish could be fixed! As this app claims to specially be made for these issues, and costs money, it’s odd to me that some of these issues exist. 

It forces you to “focus” on today’s tasks. However, I usually plan my days in advance and it won’t allow me to edit a task I added because it’s not that day currently which is quite odd and bothers my ADHD. Furthermore, I’m having issues finding tasks that i created that I don’t use everyday. I wish that I could just search them up easily and add them to a new day if I already used them before!

Other than these issues, I adore this app. I love that you can put emojis next to the tasks! I’m very visual, so this helps me a lot. However, I wish all of the emojis were available! It seems to be missing a few I wish I could put next to tasks.

I don’t want another app I waste my time on because they wanted more bells and whistles than actual features! I will always get a premium for an app that is transparent about what it can do and doesn’t try to fluff itself to justify such a large price tag for such a SIMPLE feature. title: LOVE
body: I absolutely love this app! You can customize colors icon and make it truly for you! I only have a couple small suggestions. My app I used to have, Productive, allowed me to create a shortcut from the Shortcut app. For example, when I closed my Bible app, the shortcut would run and mark my "Read Bible" task done once I confirmed it. However, I checked on shortcuts and there were no available actions for Me+. I think if you did this, it would make sense checking off tasks more efficiently when it comes to reading your bible or an audio book, or even learning a new language (I use the app Duolingo). Also, for tasks, I feel like there should be a way to slide the tasks to see a check mark, or one or two. For instance, when I drink one out of 2 bottles of water it isn't as quick as it could be to just check off 1 instead of checking off the whole task. These are just ways I thought could maybe make it more quick and efficient but otherwise I love it!!

Also, I’d like the ability to add the same task but with different reminders and times. My workweek is different than my weekends. For example, my yoga practice on Sunday will have a different start time than my practice during the workweek. 
Lastly, it’d be nice to have the option of ordering my tasks that stay the same for the days I choose so I won’t have to reorder them each day.  
Thanks so much for the app!

Well I now have to wait for that day to modify that habit. 2. Choosing a month for setting up monthly tasks. If someone wants to put a task like change furnace filters or have a medical device that has to be changed on, let’s say, 3 month cycle. It is kind of the same problem as my comment above. If they just complete that task two weeks ago and it’s a every three months, it would be nice to pick the date the schedule needs to go off of. 3. Modifying the checklist. You misspell a word or need to correct typos within a sentence, you have to delete everything to get to the spot that needs corrected. It would be nice if we can move the cursor to that spot and also have the option to move them in a different order. 4. Someone mentioned, putting a specific time of day…. Yessss. That would be soo helpful because we can easily set up notifications to help the habit. I don’t think your price is unreasonable. If you do the math, it’s 3.33 a month. Cheaper than majority of the app subscriptions out there.

title: I have recently got diagnosed with inattentive ADHD
body: Ok so I have always had trouble sticking to routines and I’ve tried many other apps and they all ask for payment and everything. The other apps didn’t work for me not even the simple todo ones due to not adding step by step details to get the job done. I don’t believe in paying for a app no matter the cost. I can have a list of everything in one place and a reminder or simply just have a list of things to do even without a time to remind me by which I like too. I like the widget option as well to put most of the list on your screen and if you check your phone often it will work better than a piece of paper which I’ve also tried. I wish there were more free templates and I like that I didn’t have to create everything from my morning routine to animal care routine and night time routine and everything between having a child and family and animals and cleaning and organizing house is a headache for me and that’s another symptom of ADHD is lack of organization and cleaning and forgetting things such as brushing teeth every day and looking after certain animals and cleaning certain things. 4 stars because I wish we had more template options and wish the entire app was free with everything in it and it’s not right to make money off of people like me and others with ADHD or just need a better routine app. With a tight budget I’m always finding the cheapest most efficient things to help me with my ADHD along with my medication. Is there a way you can make everything free on it? It would help a lot of people including me that don’t believe in paying for a app to help them.

title: Fix this please
body:
So the app seems pretty subtle at first and u do all the beginning questions for setting up ur schedule and all that. Well after u spend a good amount of time answering all the questions it says 1 week free trial 😑. Ok first of all it seems like a good app at the adds and all the reviews but they make you pay a lot for just and app that’s helps with setting better habits. Again I do know that some people don’t care abt spending the money for the app because it helps them get better habits, but most people can’t be spending that money for an app that might not even be that good. One last time I do know some of you guys will be willing to spend money for the app but nowadays inflation has made stuff very expensive and hard to pay for. Guys I know that you will think “oh it’s not that much it’s only a little money why did u download it if you knew u had to pay”, we’ll the fact is they never tell you that u have to pay for the app in the adds I know u can just look at the reviews but as someone who rarely looks at the reviews much and only looks at a few I know that some of them are fake. Lastly yall I know that you think I’m just being poor, well no just that it’s been hard these times and things are getting expensive so I’m not willing to spend the money on an app I might not even like or use. 
Ty for reading my review and for your time and yes some other people might have a different opinion than me but always make sure to read the reviews and look into an app before paying for it or downloading it.

What a pretty evil plan this is, app devs.

title: A lot of fluff and no free trial
body: The capabilities to create to-do lists is nice. Other than that, this app is filled with a lot of fluff. There are only a few workout routines. There are meditations and calming music, but you can get that anywhere. The pre-built routines are very limited, often odd, and they only look cool when you’re picking them out. Then they turn into normal tasks on your to-do list. Not those cool looking, designed pieces. The reflection prompts are very repetitive. Also, there are a lot of grammar mistakes and odd wording throughout the app. In my opinion, you can find a to-do list builder elsewhere for free. Also, they promised a free 7 day trial but I was charged in full immediately. Deleted and asked for a refund. Also, this is marketed toward people with ADHD who already struggle with impulsive purchases and the “ADHD tax”. But it isn’t super clear to a user, no guided tutorial, doesn’t seem to boast any of the science backed facts it claims it’s build off, or talk much about ADHD at all. Feels a little predatory.
author: jaybyrd7

title: Don’t do it
body:
Want to know how to use the app? Good luck. There are five whole help articles, none of which come close to explaining how to use more than one tiny piece of functionality. Want to use a feature in their screen shots? Good luck finding it.

What developer in their right mind goes through the trouble of building out an app but provides almost no help documentation? You can’t even see a DEMO of it on their website or on here. They spend more time and energy trying to recruit influencers than trying to help users.  Smacks of a MONEY and USER INFO GRAB. Until they make this app more user friendly and provide supporting documentation, I am giving this a grade of Personal info harvester. No real intent to provide real value to the user. 

I have spent 10+ days, dozens of hours trying to figure out how to do what I want to do in the app which means guess what?  I missed the free trial end date and have now paid $40 for which I still cannot use the way I intended and they provide no %^*= info on. There are five help articles that cover common sense items like how to add a widget to your Home Screen and how to change the order of your task list. 

For example, it will ask you how you are feeling seemingly randomly. It’s done that to me 2x, and only 2x, in 10 days.  I want to know how to control this.  I can’t even tell how it is triggered or review history.  I thought this app was going to allow me some kind of visualization capabilities? Analytics? Nope, none of that.  If any of this stuff exists, developer, PROVE IT. If you don’t love your own product enough to show it to your users, you clearly don’t care about whether it is used.

As far as I can tell, the only things to use this for are a handful of overplayed low value things like task lists, guided meditations, and poorly monitor sleep. You can get that for FREE in other apps!!!

title: Needs more notification control
body: Overall an awesome app, I really like the design and functionality. But there's one thing making it all a lot worse for me, and it's the amount of random notifications that come from the app, aside from the ones I set in it. I value focus very highly, and the fact I can't switch these off is pretty much counteracting the benefits I get from the app, to the point I'm probably going to uninstall it. I like my phone to bother me as little as possible and to stay present, and for an app that is built around self care, this is a huge downside to me. If the option to turn these rogue reminders off exists somewhere and I'm missing it, let me know, but not having that option is a deal breaker for me.

title: Deceptive business practices
body: They sent me a free trial and in the process of signing up for the trial they charged me for the full price of the subscription. After much back and forth between Apple Support and even trying to reach out to the developer, apparently if you supposedly had a trial before they will automatically charge you and that's that. It's very deceptive and theiving as I said because they are the ones who sent me the trial. I'm in general hesitant about trials for this reason, because I don't want to get charged without my permission, but the truth is, as a busy mom I decided to go ahead and go through with the trial and thought maybe this app would help me balance all of the things I have to juggle as a mom. So after some thought I decided to take them up on their offer for the trial. In the last step to sign up for the trial, what you think is hitting complete to finalize the trial is actually hitting complete for a payment. As I said, deceptive and poor business practices. The moment it seemed like they might have charged me. I attempted to cancel it and contact Apple support. As I said after much back-and-forth, it was determined that I had supposedly already had a trial and therefore according to them it is pretty black and white that they are just going to automatically charge me. Apple support did mention however that any app that comes from Apple that has those terms and conditions, where if you’ve had a trial before and then will be charged, it’s Apple’s policy that for theirs they atleast warn you before they charge you which this app did not do. I tried contacting the developer for resolution and they never responded. If that's their policy, they shouldn't be offering a trial, and if in offering me a trial they determine I'm not eligible for one, and they're going to charge me, that--they should put there in black and white. Even if I had a trial before and even if I knew that which I didn't, there are plenty of apps that offer multiple trials. And I would understand if I had let time relapse but it was the second it happened I tried to get resolution. The fact that I'm a busy mom worked out in their favor to decieve me and take my money and I wouldn't doubt if that's their business model and a way to make huge profits and benefit on the fact that this is something busy moms can use and count on you not knowing about having a trial prior and they count on you not knowing that in that event they'll just charge you and they know that that's a great way to steal your money and in my opinion they do that purposefully.

title: Don’t do it!
body:
I have canceled my subscription.  There are just too many issues for this to work for me.  

Please fix: 1) When time zones change, the reminder alarms do not adjust! If I am in Colorado and do something at 5am as a habit, I want that habit to be at 5am in Texas also! 2) Reminders generally don’t work - they don’t go off at all 3) entering habits took forever! Please allow tagging to be on the initial setup of the habit so you don’t have to go back in and fix it.  Allow us to edit habits that are on different days rather than just saying “focus on today’s habits.”  I was trying to input a full week routine and couldn’t do it without a hassle.  It would be nice if habits could be duplicated to put on different days at different times so you don’t have to make identical habits from scratch where the only difference is their time.  

I spent hours on this app setting it up only for the reminders not to work.  It’s frustrating and I am not spending my money on this.

title: It’s a Complete Joke
body:
Gone are the days when you could buy most apps for a one-time fee, and then support it with other small micro-transactions if you desired.

This app is a nightmare. I’m glad I’m in a relatively great place mentally or else this would have been a real let down.

With all the hoops I was jumping through shortly after downloading I knew this was a glorious mistake on my part.

That’s okay though, I learn from my mistakes.

I went to school for marketing and this hits all the wrong buttons. 

When the random slot machine started spinning (before I’d done anything) and I got the “jackpot” for 50% off I knew this was a complete scam.

Save your energy. Save your money. Look elsewhere.

The only saving grace I’ll give it is that it got me to schedule in some deep breathing using my basic Reminders app. That will be very useful over time. I have this app to thank for that.

I get it, you need to make money. We all do. It’s very hard for me to believe that these decisions for how this was designed (especially the free experience) were made to benefit your customers long term.

There’s zero proof of that to me. 

Is there short term wins as a focus? Absolutely. There’s plenty of proof of that here. Just read the other reviews.

I deleted it after the slot machine and looked at the reviews and yes this is a trend. Avoid this app.

We live in a world where most companies try to make every little app or feature a subscription. Why? Because it’s easy and preys on human psychology.

It’s way easier to sign up for a subscription than cancel it - just as it’s easier to climb a tree than come down it.

Sometimes the view is far from worth it, no matter how nice you imagine it is.

I have ADHD, and some days it’s very hard for me to feel organized or that I’m accomplishing much of anything.

This app reminded me that I can take control with the blessings already in place in my life - it’s just going to take time and patience.

That’s why I’m giving it 2 stars instead of one. I wish you all well but man this app really needs some SERIOUS work. 

I’m talking like completely starting anew and asking, “How can we really help?”, instead of just looking like you’re all trying to help.

Believe me, there is a difference.

I think you can get there but as it stands there’s no way I would ever even think of being anywhere close to this app again.

I’m thrilled that this app has helped out some people! That’s great. This isn’t for me though.

There are a few things I’m hoping to bring up to have changed/fixed:

1. I’m not able to change the time of day that my habits fall under. They all appear under “any time of day” and I’d like to be able to change them to morning, afternoon, and evening if possible. 

2. When habits are completed, the following days consistently rearrange the habits and this causes me to have to reorganize them every day. Sometimes, new habits don’t appear immediately as well.

3. The constant pop ups to pay for premium are a bit annoying honestly. Everytime the “spin the wheel” pops up, I hard reset the app and reopen because it takes too long to go through the animation just to offer me to pay for premium for the fifteeth time that day. Could you please limit the number of times the pop up occurs?

Please fix, as this app could easily be the best habit tracking app if those things were ironed out! Possibly worth paying for in the future, but not as it stands now with the issues above. 

Thanks!

title: 😬 oof
body:
Let me preface this by first saying I have autism, so I’m very used to a lot of things not working for me, simply because they weren’t made for brains that are different. However, since this app claimed to be helpful for people with ADHD (which I also have), I figured I could at least benefit from something it has to offer. Nope.  There’s a lot of flashy animation and a colorful layout, which is great to help keep the intended audience engaged long enough to make it through the beginning questionnaire portion.  However, it is not enough to distract the from the lack of useful content that is actually helpful for neurodivergent people.

The claim made within the app of it only taking 21 days to form or break a habit is a sentiment heard often, that is not actually true in the majority of scenarios. The claim most likely originated in a book written in the 1960s by a former plastic surgeon turned psychologist. The book is referencing habituation NOT habit forming, which are not the same thing. His claims were based on anecdotal information as opposed to scientific research (at least that is to be assumed since no statistical data was presented along his claims). A more recent, and better controlled study, has cited 66 days as the average. Still, it specifically points out that there was a vast range between individuals and even more so between the different types/“difficulty level” of the task (e.g. drinking water in the morning vs doing 50 sit ups a day). It also advises against putting a number on these kinds of things. It’s great to set a goal, but citing 21 days just sets people up to feel defeated at the end. 

Aside from the aforementioned, the majority of the content in the discovery tab seems to be geared toward women and people who have periods. The rest wasn’t presented in a friendly enough interface for me to even kind of want to move past the free trial period. Big yikes for the $12.99/mo paywall that makes this sparse app feel even more inadequate.

Also you can’t visually see the time frames for the routines you set, they send reminders but looking at just a blob of a list with no actual structure is also a turn off for wanting to get things done. The only thing different about this app and my head is the list is physically looking back at me and its just as overwhelming as it would be without it. 

3stars because its good at its core but could be better

title: There is a few problems…
body:
I’ve found that this app is very helpful, for reminding me every so often when I need to clean something again.It also helps keep track of the things I need to do.I love how there is still a lot of things you can use without getting any memberships. 

But…in my task list I have maybe 7 to 8 things and the tasks keep disappearing from the list and when I try to add it back it says it’s already in my task list!this is really bothering me because keeping track of my tasks is the only reason I have this app and it’s not helpful if all my tasks are disappearing! I'm not sure if anyone else has this problem but it’s a bug for me that needs to be fixed!  

Another thing is, I turned notifications on so it could remind me to do my tasks but I didn’t realize I’d be signing up to also get random “motivational” notifications throughout the day asking me how I feel and this that or the other!I wish it could just remind me about the things I need to do.

Over all it’s a pretty good app besides those few things thanks for hanging in till the end, hope the app helps you!

title: Pretty but useless
body:
App starts out with several questions and self affirming messages. Then just dumps you at a schedule screen to add items. 

You can add habits to the schedule manually or with the routine list, but if you want to edit something you’re out of luck. If it’s scheduled for a later date, you can’t touch it. So if you’d like to dust daily, you can’t. You have to wait till the dust day comes and only then can the entry be updated or removed. 

App has no user guide, explanations, YouTube guides, nothing. Even the developers website is just a list of their products and a web form to dispute billing. There is no FAQ or tutorial at all to help you get started. 

The app has several pages of healthy foods? Random meditation sound scapes? But no explanation on how it’s meant to be incorporated. 

Overall the app is a visually appealing scheduler but fails at actually acting as a scheduling app. Locking you out of updating an item if that item isn’t on todays schedule is ridiculous. And tacking on extra pages of info that isn’t actually incorporated into the app functionality just screams cramming features to get keywords for your App Store page. I can’t understand for the life of me how this app isn’t rated at 1 star like the shovelware that plainly is.

title: Promising App, But Room for Inclusive Design Improvement
body: I appreciate the app's functionality and its potential to assist me in addressing my needs and many others. Nevertheless, I can't help but notice a potential oversight in its design focus. It seems as though the app may cater primarily to women with ADHD, which doesn't fully reflect the prevalence of the condition among men. Research indicates that men with ADHD actually outnumber women by a significant margin. The design, including the choice of colors and themes, appears to lean towards a feminine aesthetic. It would be great to see more neutral color options and themes, as well as an equal representation of both male and female characters. As a user, I hope for a more inclusive experience that doesn't make me feel out of place.

title: Temporary Review if Fixed (Update)
body:
Today marks day one of my 7-day free trial. I was so excited to download this app because the reviews seemed pretty good. However I was hesitant because There were some concerns about glitches reported. I literally just downloaded this app one hour prior to writing this review. The app seems amazing if all you he bugs are fixed! I ran into an issue where I was trying to set up my routines, and there is a glitch that prevents you from customizing the days , weeks, etc. if you change the default dates, it’s not letting you add the routine, but it shows that it was added. So the routine basically disappears into thin air. You can’t find it anywhere! But when you check in the routine catalog, it shows that it was added . This is so frustrating. even more frustrating, because it shows that it was added… And it isn’t added (it’s somewhere in purgatory) this app will not let you add it again, nor will it let you delete it to try to add again. So I had to contact support to try to rectify. For example, I want to add a workout routine for the gym for M/Tu/Th. The default shows S/M/Tu/W/Th/F. Whenever I change the default dates to my custom dates, it does not appear in my routine list. I also noticed that the workout routine category is completely missing from the routines list. I tried to troubleshoot it by creating a new category, but was not successful in doing so. The only way I could add it is by allowing it to show the wrong routine days. That is counterproductive to the use of this app. Because now it’ll show that I am not completing routines or that I’m not productive because it’s set up for incorrect days. Another issue, which I think is a huge issue, once a routine is added from the routine catalog, you cannot remove it. That is bananas to me! Why is that a limited feature?? this came up with the workout routines that could not show up in my routine, but it showed up in the catalog area that it was added. And there is absolutely no way to correct this. That’s weird. The app has a plus sign next to each routine to add it to your routine list, wouldn’t it make sense to have a subtract sign to remove it? Why is this not already a feature as popular as this app is? Again, I’m excited to try it out, but within the first hour I’ve run into these issues. So if these issues aren’t fixed by the time, my trial ends, I will not cancel my purchase of the full year as plan. I’ll be happy to update this review if these glitches are fixed. So if this review remains… That will indicate that the developers did not address this issue.

UPDATE:
The issue was resolved. Not sure if it was an intended fix or if the glitch cleared itself. But I was able to add and delete customized routine activities so I changed the rating from 1 start to 4. It really is a nice app. The reason I gave it a 4 and decided to no longer pay for it is because you can’t organize your activities I in order. Even when I change the order for my morning activities, it goes out of order the next day. So I kept having to rearrange the order daily. Which caused me to miss checking off some completed activities because it was out of order on the bottom of the list. It would be great if this could be fixed. I would definitely consider paying for the year of the app had this feature. It’s small but makes a world of difference especially if you’re short on time.

title: The ultimate task teacher and organizer
body:
As a young adult, one of the biggest challenges is understanding the frequency and importance of day to day tasks because some tasks you don’t notice until it is a large problem or is such a mess it needs to be addressed. This app has helped me build a plan to stay ahead of these tasks and do them in a consistent rotation where days off of work spent cleaning don’t exist anymore now I I have 1 hour worth of productive throughout the day set up for building good habits automatically. From mentally stimulating things like staying consistent in reading, to day to day responsibilities such as doing a different deep clean every day on a bi weekly rotation of 14 different tasks. This organization is amazing and it take tremendous mental strain off of myself as I no longer am always on alert looking for what I am forgetting and if I do stumble across something that isn’t on the to do lists I can add it in the moment and pick how often I want that task done. So all in all the app is amazing if you are having trouble building consistent cleaning, self care, fitness, and productivity habits

Only critique 
I wish there was an easier way to find a total list of tasks so me and my significant other have an easier time picking days for daily, weekly, and monthly tasks as we are trying to rotate the ones we don’t enjoy so we can work better as a team while not needing to talk about our to do list every morning and night. Also an annual/ bi annual category planning option would be awesome for setting up things like car maintenance taxes school dues for the kids etcetera.

Thanks to the developers 
Thank you for making an app that allows me to find joy in tasks that used to stress me out as the organization was overwhelming

title: Not free and not helpful.
body:
I’m glad I read more than the first glowing reviews. 
This app will offer you a free trial that you have to commit to pay at the end. I know many of you are like me and will forget to cancel it. 
Once I said no to the trial any time I wanted to look at or start a routine it flashed offers for a paid subscription. This happened at least ten times in a row before I decided it just wasn’t worth it. 
This app is a trap for people with adhd. It offers shiny features that lure us in and then forces you to pay with the promise of more productivity.

title: This is great when you get overwhelmed or need motivation!
body:
I love this app! I’ve been using for a little over two weeks now and use it everyday. I accidentally got the subscription (forgot to cancel before the trial ended) BUT I’m glad I did! I do a lot of my morning routine now thanks to this app and the little reminders and affirmations are always nice. 

My only critiques are:
- I wish you could see a list of ALL your tasks and adjust them when you want. I’ve accidentally scheduled one at a later date and I can’t go in and edit it until the day of. I get that we should focus on the here and now but I don’t think /not/ seeing a master list of your tasks is necessary. For example, the days I work out have changed due to my own schedule changing from today onwards but my work out task isn’t until tomorrow so I can’t go in and change it. 

- more color and icon options for tasks - I love the variety now but wish I could just choose my own from my phone

title: PLEASE READ BEFORE GETTING APP!!!
body: As much as I love the thought of this app I just can’t seem to really find anything that I like about it. Yes, you can plan out your morning routine and yes you can set goals for yourself but how it is all set up is just confusing. When you log into the app, you don’t have your full on morning routine there, you just have all your goals which causes you to click around on a few things to find your morning routine and you have to set it up yourself (causing you to probably just make a schedule that WONT be used and will not fit your needs to help achieve your goals) with limited options to add to it and if you set reminders it doesn’t always remind you. Plus, when you try to set up a workout routine, most of the little workout videos are locked. (And by most I mean all) And the only way to unlock them is if you pay the monthly subscription which yeah is only about $1.70 but honestly I just wanted an app that could help me with my goals and getting better at being more productive so paying was NOT something I had in mind. And it’s not just the workouts that are locked, it’s a LOT of the things on this app that are locked. PLUS, I HATE that every time I open up the app I am greeted with a wheel to spin that decides whether or not I get a discount on the monthly subscription. WHICH RIGHT NOW IT SAYS $1.70 BUT IN REALITY THATS %50 OFF!!! So $1.70 is NOT the monthly subscription. Again I like the concept of this app and I definitely think that there could be some changes to how it’s set up and what not but right now it’s just not working for me.

title: Great app for adhd, ocd, add, ect.
body: I have adhd and struggle with getting things done but this app helps so much. You can plan out your day or you can just make a list of things that you need to get done. It’s free, add free, and you can also pay only 1.70$ a month for premium wich is very affordable. You can also set goals like do this this this many times today and you can create your own step by step checklist. With my adhd I often can’t get things done because I can’t focus or because I don’t know where to start or I’ll get stressed by all the stuff I have to do but with this app I can just do things step by step, little by little. I I’ve had this app for not even two days but my mental health is already improving and I’m genuinely so much happier and more productive. So for anyone looking at the reviews seeing if they should get it or not, this app is a ten out of ten and you should definitely get it. Big thanks to the creators of this app for improving my lifestyle.

title: Unfortunately not worth the price
body:
Pros:

Attractive app
Easy to use

Cons:

Limited emoji options for tasks; no skin tone option

Too much focus on hashtags, social media ambassadors. Focus on making a fully functional app that functions as described and for the advertised population before being concerned with “ambassadors”. 

Limited color selection; all pastels

title: Lulls you in thinking you can do anything. All paid
body:
Don’t believe the reviewer trying to claim you don’t need to pay to use this. You absolutely do. I was excited to try this. I had a feeling something was up because the little intro quiz was very long and thorough. Which was a sign it was purposefully trying to invest you into it to just give in an buy it by the end. And sure enough as soon as I got to the actual app, not only was it a CONSTANT barrage of ‘buy buy buy’ pop ups, but you could do virtually nothing for free. No useful free planner options. Basically everything that would make this useful you can’t do. I would expect that it would be like any other good app in that it had a few basic ones free, or a limited amount that you could use. But no. NOTHING.
Honestly just stick to any of the other habit planner apps. They at least don’t try to lull you in like this. The ONLY good thing about this app is the fact it has inclusive options for how to be referred to. But still an immediate delete. Really a shame too cause it seemed to have nice planner options. Too bad none are usable.

title: NOPE.  Absolutely NOT!
body:
Not sure who developed this APP, but I get the impression that it was not done appropriately with a person with ADHD.  The biggest challenge to ADHD is being in the moment.  So to bring someone into the moment with such a great app idea woulld require that app being on and synced across iCloud.  This app does not sync with iCloud.  That is a fundamental flaw in the app.  And it's ashame becuase this app seems to hit the mark in a lot of places.  

I have alreay submitted an email to support about this.  But I will be deleting this app and ending my trial ... which began only a few hours ago.

VERY DISAPOINTING for someone who is struggling to organize their life.  

Also, If the app is 4 yrs. old, why has only one person reviewd it prior to me it?  I wonder if it was someone the developr knos.  Food for thought.

title: Dark patterns targeting people in need of help. FTC take note.
body:
After answering a few questions it prompts you to do a “free trial” of premium without actually explaining what premium offers vs using it for free. It wasn’t until it tried to access my payment information, despite saying no payment was required, that I realized something was up.

If you close the trial prompt with the tiny, hard-to-spot x in the corner it shows a prerendered video of a wheel giving the illusion that you have “won” a 50% discount on premium and a one-minute timer starts to pressure you into accepting without having time to think, preying on the impulse of FOMO. What it doesn't tell you is that accepting your “prize” charges you immediately without any free trial.

Absolutely not worth it. Don’t trust the positive reviews.

To the devs, before they can give their canned reply to this: I don't care how small your team is. If you really want to work on improving start by not trying to trick people looking to improve their lives out of their money.

title: Just a glorified to-do list
body:
I was incredibly underwhelmed by this app. Most of the pre-made routines are just silly. One of them, ‘Expanding Your Social Circle,’ includes the task “Try to fall in love.” With no further explanation or directions. Another, ‘Try On New Years’ Hot Springs’ is particularly odd. The title looks like a bad translation, the concept is pretty niche, and the elements in the routine are broad and (again) contain no extra help or direction. 
Overall, the routines are broken down into overly broad and generic steps. With ADHD, that can be overwhelming and more hassle than it’s worth to customize it. If you are hoping for an app that breaks down large tasks into clear, approachable, bite-sized steps, this app is definitely not for you. Certainly not worth the $40 annual subscription price.

title: Not What I Was Expecting...
body:
I tried out this app months ago when I was trying to find apps to better plan my life. At some point, I uninstalled since I did not have enough funds to go with a subscription at the time. I came back today and the features that once were there that I liked are no longer there. I also find it a ton more clunky and more stressful to set tasks up. It's easier to do it on another app I use on top of it having a Lifetime purchase option. It does a way better job at planning while being minimalistic. The planning app I use currently may not have some of the features this app has, but at least the experience is more smooth and less stressful to use. I accidentally subscribed while trying to get to my homescreen to check something unfortunately. I'll be getting my refund once for sure once I am able to.

I do not recommend the app if you are looking for a smooth task creating experience. It doesn't even list ALL DEFAULT tags either when you make a custom task which I find ridiculous. I am unable to set the custom task to the Relax tag due to this... There are other apps that perform better than this app in terms of task-creating experience. If you are looking for templates and small things to improve your routine though, then this app might work for you. For me, personally, it's just too clunky and unpleasant to create my tasks properly. The app also no longer has the features I find that stands out and what I look for either.

TLDR Version: App is too clunky with planning and creating the tasks are unpleasant. Many of the features that I liked have been removed. Recommended for those who enjoy templates and for those new to planning. Not recommended for those who are looking for an organized, pleasant task-creating experience.

title: Not actually for ADHD.
body:
As a general rule I hate when people prey on neurodivergent people anyways, but I gave this a try because of some other reviews.

 I loved the intro to this app, the questions really made me think there was something to it but they are actually just more of a survey to show you which “routine” might be best for you in a grand list of routines you still have to look through on your own. It’s not custom or tailored like they make you believe. 

Then comes the catch that you have to pay in order to use the app and I cannot get behind any companies that use someone’s disorder as a marketing scheme. It’s disgusting. 

The final straw for me was that it was so difficult to use. You can add routines all you want but you can not remove them, you have to individually go to each item and take it off. The juice was not worth the squeeze here for me and actually having ADHD I already lost interest and deleted the ap. 

Overall, there are better, more user friendly, ACTUALLY FREE apps out there if you are actually trying to find a way to keep track of your routines and habits.

title: Can’t Honestly Evaluate
body:
I left 3 stars just because I will never know what this app is like, since in order to try it I had to commit to a subscription. The market is way too saturated with self-care and motivation these days, and there is just too much out there, to take a risk on purchasing without knowing the quality of what I’m committing to. I have had enough situations where apps charge me needlessly or even dishonestly, that the risk of signing up is too great for me to take a chance on what could be a great app. 

My advice is to do what a lot of other apps do that are insanely successful now (and I regularly subscribe to), and allow free usage for a few days, perhaps even in a limited fashion, where you only get access to parts of it, and then ask for me to subscribe, after I’ve already been inside the app and know what exactly I’m signing up for. There is zero way of me knowing what this even is. Why on earth would I subscribe to something I’m not even sure what it offers? 

Okay, rant over. That’s all. :)

body:
I have ADD and this looked like it would be a great tool to help me to better organize. There are routines you can add like exercise, clean, sleep, etc. However, you can’t customize them. I’m recovering from a calf injury so I can’t run right now but I would like a way to add the plan my PT gave me to follow. 

Also, from an ADD perspective, the tasks are very disorganized which makes it very difficult to follow any sort of plan for the day. There are also tasks to NOT do something, like drink alcohol. Also, some of the tasks are written not grammatically correct; “Laundry the dish towels” and “Taking exercise a priority”.

The thing that was the nail in the coffin is that I’m not able to cancel this subscription. I go to my settings, Apple account, subscriptions and then click on “cancel subscription” for this app. However, it’s doesn’t do anything. It doesn’t cancel.

title: Good
body:
So… For the most part, it’s well designed, mostly intuitive, thoughtful, easy to get started with lots of preset schedule ideas, how-tos, resources, and so forth. 

But the current issues I’ve been having since the latest iOS update kind of killed it for me. I’m autistic and ADHD. So while this was helpful for organizing my days, the problems just started feeling too overwhelming.

 Like the audio disruptions; clicking/sound cutting out on other apps while Me+ was open in the background. Alerts going bonkers and repeating 3, 4, 5 times or more all at once. The alarm failing to go off if Me+ wasn’t the app “currently in use.” It’s supposed to be running in the background for the alarm to work, but that stopped being enough at some point and it wasn’t going off until I was already awake (as much as an hour and 15 minutes past the alarm time) and had unlocked the phone to turn off the iOS alarm(s) and check other apps/alerts. 

It also likes to hijack the audio while the alarm is sounding, which is horrible for sensory issues first thing in the morning. Or even 4th thing… Couldn’t figure out a way to stop the alarm after hitting “snooze” to silence the full-volume alarm sounds (so I could think strait without my brain oozing out my ears). 😵‍💫 I get that it’s meant to prevent us from just turning it off in our sleep, and help jog the brain awake, but there needs to be a, “I’m already awake, standing in my living room, and don’t feel like stopping mid-morning-routine to do your stupid puzzles,” button or something. 

Ended up just triggering my demand avoidance instead of helping, after a point. “Dothething! Dothething! Dothething!” Alert overload. Too many things yelling at me that I have to “do the thing,” not enough things checking in gently. 

Bummer. It’s otherwise a great app. I suspect it just needs some refining so it plays nice with iOS. I paid for a whole year, but ended up deleting the app so… that’s a little frustrating. 

I’ll check back later I guess, see if anything’s working better. But in the meantime, I can’t handle the glitches. (I did email about most of what’s mentioned here, but there was no reply.)

title: Be careful with "free trial" and "spin for sales"
body:
I'm glad that the people who like this app do, but it definitely is not for me. I like you can color code (I'm a nerd) but the color palette is limited and some colors are very close upon first glance. Making checklists and routines should be easier, especially since this is marketed towards those of us with adhd. Major flaw is you can only access routines on the day they are set up. If it's Monday and you want to go ahead and check off tasks that are assigned to Wednesday, a message pops up that says "let's concentrate on today" and other random messages.     If you want to rearrange tasks or the day you do them be prepared to delete your entire routine and start from scratch. 
You have to answer questions then agree to the free trial before you can even get into the app and play  around in it to see if you want it. I declined the free trial but then a wheel comes up with sale prices so I figured if I got a free month I would try it. I spun 50% off a year- I didn't want to commit to a year, but when I clicked the screen thinking I was  just moving past that point it "accepted the offer" and I was charged $20 right then. I made sure to go into subscriptions immediately and cancel the auto renewal. I can handle wasting $20, but I am very grateful I didn't waste $40.

title: Be Aware!
body:
I installed this app months ago just to check it out and see if it would really help me. However, I couldn't figure it out, and after playing with the app for a few hours, I got tired and decided to remove it. Then, a few days later, I noticed that I had been charged for a one-year premium plan without receiving any prior notification. I sent an email to the support team, explaining the situation and mentioning that I didn't have the app on my phone and had no knowledge of the upcoming payment. Their response was simply, "We are very sorry for the inconvenience, but there's nothing we can do. You can request a refund from the App Store!" Unfortunately, they did not provide a refund.

I'm mentioning this issue now because I've been searching for an app to help organize my life and came across this app again. Despite my previous negative experiences, I thought I would give it another try and see if it could be useful for me. However, just like the first time, it is not practical for me to use. It might be helpful for someone else, though, but it serves as a reminder of how unfairly they treated me.

If you also have ADHD, be cautious of falling into the same trap... if you know what I mean!!

title: ADHD and Depression helper
body:
I like using this app as a habit tracker. 

As someone with ADHD and depression, this app helps remind and motivate me to do basic tasks each day. I’m often terrible at remembering if I’ve taken my meds and this app has helped me stay consistent with taking them. When in a depressive episode, basic tasks like washing my face & brushing my teeth can fall to the wayside. This app helps motivate me & remind me to do those basic tasks. Being able to check off one small task like washing your face when in a depressive episode can feel like a huge accomplishment. 

My one pet peeve is that the widget does not refresh on its own. I also wish the data review for tracking habits was more user friendly and visually appealing like the “Habit” app. 

As for the other parts of the app, there are definitely flaws and room for improvement. There are typos in the quotes, the workouts don’t load, the alarm doesn’t always work, and the processes aren’t streamlined.

title: Great idea, but needs some improvements
body:
I have used the app for 3 days so far, and I really enjoy it. It offers different routines to pick and choose from, you can alter the details and add to do lists within the tasks you select. I also like they provide journals and wellness tutorials like stretches etc. It is very helpful to someone starting out in personal wellness.

My suggestions to improve the app:
- Allow back dated mood entries. My day typically ends around 10pm/11pm, so when I go to do my daily reflection it may be beyond midnight. This posts for the current day, not the day prior, and there is no way to adjust it, that I know of.
- Allow adjustments to future to do lists. I try to edit or adjust chores in the following days, and I get a purple bar that tells me to "focus on today". It is a bit annoying, and I tend to forget things easily (hence why I have this app) and that would be really beneficial to me if I could adjust things as I think about it, whether it be a day or a week from now. If there is a way to do this, it would be helpful to have an easier way of doing it.

Thank you for the app, I really appreciate the thoughtfulness that has gone into the apps creation and mood. The app is a very positive space and I look forward to using it as time goes on!

title: Amazing app only one complaint. Still worth it though
body:
Pros:
helps me break down tasks
Helps me stay organized 
Helps me see areas where I’m struggling 
Constant reminders are amazing. 
It makes it easier for me to plan out my week 
If I forget a task it’s easy to go back and look at what needs to be completed. 

Cons: 
1. The alarm feature. I use music to go to sleep at night, and I play it over my Bluetooth speaker. When the alarm goes off it suddenly increases the volume of the speaker and you cannnnot turn it down until you complete your wake up tasks. I’m a light sleeper and this causes me to jerk awake in a panic because suddenly there is this loud noise. I hate it. 

2. Adding tasks and customizing the frequency. I had to readjust the frequency of tasks multiple times after I saved them. It’s annoying but it doesn’t take away from the usability. 

Overall I think it’s a great app especially if you’re neurodivergent. Give it a try!

title: Unusable without premium
body:
Definitely feels like some of these reviews are disingenuous.

1. Very deceptive, predatory, and dark UX patterns throughout the application onboarding to force people into paying for premium.

1a. The initial onboarding directs you to create a habit plan from a template. When you hit save, the app cycles shows a pop-up for 50% off premium. Hitting cancel (hidden at the top) takes you back to your unsaved habits. You are NEVER able to save that template as the app cycles through 3-4 pop-ups for the same discount, including an annoying 10-15 second jackpot wheel that can’t be canceled)

3. Really don’t see the value in paying for something that other applications do for free

title: Great app but need some updates
body:
Honestly I downloaded the app because I preferred the structure and theme compared to similar apps on the appstore and I’m glad I did download the app! To get most of the app you do need to subscribe to an annual subscription though but I believe it is worth it! There are many features available on the app that can’t be found in other similar apps such as a sleep tracker, sleeping aids (rain sounds in the background/ story audios/ etc), journals for several different topics, and gym/workout guides!:) 
I am quite happy with my experience so far but there needs to be some updates that maximise efficiency and just make sense.
1. If a habit repeats throughout the day, there needs to be the option to set several reminders/notifications for each periodic habit. 
2. There needs to either be a library of all habits created where you can go in and edit as you please, or enable users to go on other days of the week and edit their habits there instead of getting the alert “let’s focus on todays habit” that inhibits them from altering any habit that may not be a daily occurrence.
3. I find that notifications and reminders aren’t consistent. Some habits I get my daily notifications but others I don’t, I’m still trying to figure out why this is but if the creators can look into the issue that would be great! 
Overall I am pleased with this app and I do see the app does get consistent updates so I will stick with it and hopefully these issues will get resolved in due time :)

body:

I downloaded this as free trial got frustrated and closed the app to never open it again until today. I paid $39.99 for an app I haven’t touched since the day I downloaded it months ago. Out of sight out of mind is a real problem for me. 
I stopped using this app immediately because I could not edit my future routine. When I originally set it up I made mistakes I could not fix until the day of that routine. Today I saw another add and decided to see if they had fixed this. I’m disappointed to see even after the update I still can not reset or edit my routine. The last time I tried this app I was on a 3rd shift schedule and now I am on a second shift. That is a drastic change in lifestyle yet I cant do something as simple as changing my task for the entire week? 

I already paid $40 for this thing so I am going to go through and edit each day as it comes up and give the idea a real chance. 

Please ad a way to edit my entire routine or at least a way to entirely reset it so I can rebuild it. 

Adding a monthly payment plan will help as well. $40 is an awful lot to some people for an app that in reality you could accomplish with a daily checklist. To me it was just annoying but for someone else it could impact their groceries for next week.

title: Best App I’ve Downloaded-ADHD Win!
body: Unlike countless other planner apps out there you don’t have to pay to actually be able to use the app. You wont believe how happy it makes me that you don’t need a subscription to be able to plan out your life. I personally find it disgusting and discouraging that loads of other apps take advantage of the challenges neurodivergent people face when they are just trying to make their life a bit easier and more organized. This app offers so many capabilities without having to pay. You can make checklists under activities and events. It gives you suggestions of things to add to your schedule. Events/activities are very customizable. It has a list of routines to try from hot spring to-dos to work out and cleaning routines. You can set alarms, track your sleep, listen to soundscapes and meditations, and check broadcasts. Broadcasts includes a great overview of how you slept including percentages of when you woke up during the night and when you were in light sleep and deep sleep. It also has sound recordings of your night. Weather in your area and fun history facts. They also give out free or discounted membership opportunities. It’s honestly a great experience and I feel more confident and in control of my schedule than ever before!

author: Mmm... Qué pasa?

title: Limited and Profit-Driven
body:
The application is incredibly limited without a subscription, which is disappointing for those who may not have the financial means to purchase one.

Furthermore, the pre-created routines offered by the application are limited and not tailored to individual needs, which defeats the purpose of using such an app. Instead of providing a range of helpful and customizable routines, the application only offers a few basic routines that you can add to your plan AFTER you buy the subscription.

This approach not only limits the usefulness of the app, but it also seems to prioritize profit over the needs of the ADHD community. It is important to create an environment where individuals with ADHD can thrive, and an application that requires payment for basic features does not foster such an environment.

Overall, I would not recommend this application to anyone looking to improve their ADHD symptoms. With limited routines and a focus on profit, this app falls short of what is needed to support those with ADHD.

Secondly the ability to edit future dates needs to be added instead of asking to focus on today (most people plan for the week or month all at once and do not have time to edit their schedule daily). Thirdly when editing the details of a task it should not reset the task and erase any previous data related to that task. Fourthly there has been several times I have gotten into the app and all the tasks are gone. Finally maybe there should be a way to set more than 1 reminder for tasks that have a goal of more than once a day. Again the app has potential to be useful and great but it’s lil things that will ruin it.

title: Awesome App!
body: Having ADD I can truthfully say this is the best productivity app I’ve tried. So many others force you to create your routines, habits and schedules all by yourself. Most productivity apps start in a place of customization. By the time you figure out what schedule you want to choose, when you want to do it and how often you lose momentum it’s so exhausting you want to quit. The beauty of this app is that there are routine templates based on who you are and what you want to achieve and then you just add those goals/routines it to your custom one. Just the right amount of free choice but mixed so much with outlines that are pre-set you don’t have to figure a lot out. Definitely recommend - worth the hype. My only suggestion/request if possible would be to add a goal template that includes pets. When to walk them, spend time with them, take them to the vet, get them groomed. No points taken off though - this is awesome!

title: Almost there! But some issues
body:
I’ve been using this app for a few weeks, my mom is paying for my premium subscription and also has it on her phone.

The app is great, it’s been helping me keep track of my habits because I have ADHD and struggle with productivity, it also documents daily mood stats and reflections, every night I look forward to opening the app and checking off what I’ve done and reflecting on my day and documenting my mood. 

However I’ve had some issues, two days ago I opened the app and saw that all of my habits had disappeared and my habit stats disappeared too, I had to manually re-add all my habits and apparently my original habits aren’t completely gone because when I tried to re-add one of them it tells me that the habit already exists, but is nowhere to be found. My mood stats were untouched and still there, but that brings me to my next issue.

When it hits 12 am, you can’t go back to add your mood stat from the day before, you can go back on previous days in your habit stats to check off things you forgot to check off in the moment, but with mood stats you can’t do that, so if you forgot to document your mood for the day and it hits 12 then you’re out of luck. It’s my biggest pet peeve with this app, sometimes I don’t have the time/don’t remember to check things off immediately, it isn’t an issue with the habit stats but with mood stats you can’t do anything about it.

title: April 2023 Update
body:
Purchased the app in January, lost all date in April and the Data Repair feature did not work. I’m going to add all my tasks back and give it one more go, I’ll update if it happens again. 

Overall, I still feel it is the best habit building widget. Streaks is a close second. Streaks allows you to choose which habits to include and you can have multiple widgets with different habits. 

If you aren’t looking to utilize the widget, I would pass on this app. They spend way too much time on the Discover tab and other tabs that I have a hard time believing anyone is using. The premade habits are mostly nonsense. Check them out during your free trial and you’ll see what I mean. The widget is what sets this app apart from others. 

Biggest areas for improvement (as of 4/23) are:

1. No good way to have a task be a certain amount of times per week or month without being day of the week specific. For example, maybe you want to exercise 5 times per week but don’t want to commit to certain days, or want to do something weather-dependent or once a month and it doesn’t matter the day. It would be amazing if there was a widget for daily tasks, another for weekly tasks, and another for monthly tasks.

2. You cannot backdate tasks, even by a day. This isn’t a huge deal but is annoying. Maybe you start a habit and it makes you feel good so the next day you add it as something to continue but you want to give yourself credit for doing it yesterday. You can’t. Also if you start something like “brush my teeth” as a habit midweek, in the widget it’s going to look like you just didn’t do that until midweek. Also wish it would let you pick which day of the week to start it on, or at least the option of starting the week on Monday. (It’s Sunday to Saturday.)

3. In the widget, if you only have a task set to a certain day, on that day, it will show in your widget and it will show like you didn’t do the task on the days it was not assigned. It needs to be shaded in. 

I feel like the type of people who would use this app long term are list makers and visual people and probably a lot of perfectionists and it would be a lot more motivating to continue use of those items were fixed.
